Aldol Condensation.question: Which of the following base catalysts is most typically used for carrying out standard Aldol Condensation of ethanal?
Aldol Condensation.explanation: Aldol condensation requires a dilute base like $\text{dil. NaOH}$ or $\text{Ba(OH)}_2$ to generate enolate ions without causing resinification or Cannizzaro reaction.

Aldol Condensation.question: What is the mandatory structural prerequisite for a carbonyl compound to undergo self-Aldol Condensation?

options.text: Presence of at least one $\alpha$-hydrogen atom
Presence of an aromatic ring adjacent to carbonyl group

Aldol Condensation.explanation: The base must deprotonate the $\alpha$-carbon to generate a nucleophilic enolate; thus at least one $\alpha$-hydrogen is strictly mandatory.

Aldol Condensation.question: Which of the following carbonyl compounds CANNOT undergo self-aldol condensation?
Aldol Condensation.explanation: Benzaldehyde has no $\alpha$-hydrogens attached to the carbonyl group and therefore cannot form an enolate to undergo self-aldol condensation.

Aldol Condensation.question: What is the major organic product formed when ethanal is warmed with dilute $\text{NaOH}$ followed by heating?
Aldol Condensation.explanation: Ethanal dimerizes to 3-hydroxybutanal (aldol), which upon heating eliminates a molecule of water to give but-2-enal (crotonaldehyde).

Aldol Condensation.question: When propan-2-one (acetone) is treated with $\text{Ba(OH)}_2$ followed by heating, the major $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated ketone formed is:
Aldol Condensation.explanation: Acetone forms 4-hydroxy-4-methylpentan-2-one (diacetone alcohol), which on heating loses water to yield 4-methylpent-3-en-2-one (mesityl oxide).

Aldol Condensation.question: What is the key reactive intermediate involved in the base-catalyzed aldol addition step?
Aldol Condensation.explanation: Deprotonation of the $\alpha$-hydrogen by base yields a resonance-stabilized enolate anion $[\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{O}^- \leftrightarrow ^-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}=\text{O}]$, which acts as the nucleophile.

Aldol Condensation.question: The dehydration of a $\beta$-hydroxy aldehyde or ketone (aldol product) under heating proceeds predominantly via which mechanism?
Aldol Condensation.explanation: Due to the acidic $\alpha$-proton adjacent to carbonyl and poor leaving group ($\text{OH}^-$), dehydration of aldols occurs via the $\text{E1cB}$ (Elimination Unimolecular Conjugate Base) pathway.

Aldol Condensation.question: Why do $\beta$-hydroxy carbonyl compounds dehydrate much more readily than normal simple alcohols?

options.text: The $\text{C}-\text{O}$ bond in aldols is significantly weaker than a normal single bond
Hydroxide ion is an extremely good leaving group under all neutral conditions
Aldols are inherently anti-aromatic prior to dehydration
The resulting $\text{C}=\text{C}$ double bond is in conjugation with the carbonyl group, providing substantial thermodynamic resonance stabilization

Aldol Condensation.explanation: The driving force for dehydration is the formation of a conjugated $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated enone/enal system with lower overall free energy.

Aldol Condensation.question: The reaction between an aromatic aldehyde lacking $\alpha$-hydrogens and an aliphatic aldehyde or ketone possessing $\alpha$-hydrogens in dilute alkali is specifically known as:
Aldol Condensation.explanation: Claisen-Schmidt condensation is the crossed aldol condensation between an aromatic aldehyde (e.g., benzaldehyde) and an aliphatic aldehyde/ketone.

Aldol Condensation.question: When an equimolar mixture of benzaldehyde and acetophenone is treated with dilute $\text{NaOH}$, the major product obtained after heating is:
Aldol Condensation.explanation: Acetophenone forms the enolate, which attacks the more electrophilic benzaldehyde carbonyl carbon. Dehydration then yields chalcone (1,3-diphenylprop-2-en-1-one).

Aldol Condensation.question: When benzaldehyde reacts with excess acetone in dilute $\text{NaOH}$ in a 2:1 molar ratio, the final conjugated condensation product is:
Aldol Condensation.explanation: Acetone has two $\alpha$-methyl groups. Both undergo crossed aldol condensation with two molecules of benzaldehyde to give dibenzalacetone.

Aldol Condensation.question: When an equimolar mixture of ethanal ($\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$) and propanal ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$) is treated with dilute $\text{NaOH}$, how many distinct structural condensation products are theoretically formed?
Aldol Condensation.explanation: Each aldehyde can form an enolate and each can act as an electrophile, giving 2 self-aldol products (crotonaldehyde, 2-methylpent-2-enal) and 2 cross-aldol products (2-methylbut-2-enal, pent-2-enal).

Aldol Condensation.question: What is the major product obtained when hexane-2,5-dione is treated with dilute aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ followed by heating?
Aldol Condensation.explanation: Intramolecular aldol condensation favors the formation of a stable, unstrained 5-membered conjugated cyclopentenone ring rather than a strained 3-membered ring.

Aldol Condensation.question: What is the product formed from the intramolecular aldol condensation of heptane-2,6-dione upon treatment with base and heat?
Aldol Condensation.explanation: Enolate formation at C-1 attacks C-6 carbonyl to form a thermodynamically stable 6-membered conjugated enone (3-methylcyclohex-2-en-1-one).

Aldol Condensation.question: Which of the following compounds gives crotonaldehyde when treated with dilute $\text{NaOH}$ followed by heat?
Aldol Condensation.explanation: $2\text{CH}_3\text{CHO} \xrightarrow{\text{dil. NaOH}} \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CHO} \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CHCHO}$ (crotonaldehyde).

Aldol Condensation.question: Treatment of cyclohexanone with dilute $\text{NaOH}$ upon heating yields which major conjugated product?
Aldol Condensation.explanation: Cyclohexanone enolate attacks another cyclohexanone molecule, followed by dehydration to yield 2-(cyclohex-1-en-1-yl)cyclohexan-1-one.

Aldol Condensation.question: Which of the following aldehydes yields 2-ethylhex-2-enal upon self-aldol condensation followed by dehydration?
Aldol Condensation.explanation: $2\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CHO} \xrightarrow{\text{base, } \Delta} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}=\text{C(CH}_2\text{CH}_3)\text{CHO}$ (2-ethylhex-2-enal).

Aldol Condensation.question: In the aldol condensation between propanal and ethanal, if ethanal acts solely as the electrophilic acceptor and propanal acts as the nucleophile (enolate), the product after dehydration is:
Aldol Condensation.explanation: Propanal enolate attacks ethanal: $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO} + ^-\text{CH(CH}_3)\text{CHO} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH(CH}_3)\text{CHO} \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{C(CH}_3)\text{CHO}$ (2-methylbut-2-enal).

Aldol Condensation.question: Why does 2,2-dimethylpropanal (pivalaldehyde) fail to undergo self-aldol condensation?

options.text: The carbonyl group is completely unreactive towards nucleophilic addition
The $\alpha$-carbon is fully substituted (quaternary) and lacks any $\alpha$-hydrogen
It exists entirely in the enol tautomeric form

Aldol Condensation.explanation: Pivalaldehyde is $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{CHO}$. The $\alpha$-carbon has no hydrogens, preventing enolate formation.

Aldol Condensation.question: What is the stereochemical configuration of the double bond predominantly formed in the dehydration step of aldol condensation?

options.text: A racemic mixture of optical enantiomers
Equal 1:1 mixture of $(E)$ and $(Z)$ isomers under all conditions
$(E)$-alkene (trans) due to lower steric hindrance and higher thermodynamic stability

Aldol Condensation.explanation: The trans $(E)$-isomer is thermodynamically more stable due to minimized steric repulsion between bulky substituents.

Aldol Condensation.question: Consider the sequence: $\text{HC}\equiv\text{CH} \xrightarrow{\text{dil. } \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 / \text{HgSO}_4} A \xrightarrow{\text{dil. NaOH, } \Delta} B$. What is compound $B$?
Aldol Condensation.explanation: Hydration of ethyne produces ethanal ($A$), which undergoes aldol condensation upon treatment with dilute $\text{NaOH}$ and heat to give crotonaldehyde ($B$).

Aldol Condensation.question: Consider the sequence: $\text{CH}_3\text{C}\equiv\text{CH} \xrightarrow{\text{dil. } \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 / \text{HgSO}_4} A \xrightarrow{\text{Ba(OH)}_2, \Delta} B$. What is compound $B$?
Aldol Condensation.explanation: Propyne hydrates via Markovnikov addition to acetone ($A$), which undergoes self-aldol condensation and dehydration to give mesityl oxide ($B$).

Aldol Condensation.question: Which of the following compounds gives a positive iodoform test AND also undergoes aldol condensation?
Aldol Condensation.explanation: Acetone contains a methyl ketone group ($-\text{COCH}_3$) giving positive iodoform test, and has $\alpha$-hydrogens allowing aldol condensation.

Aldol Condensation.question: What is the role of an acid catalyst (e.g., dry $\text{HCl}$) in acid-catalyzed aldol condensation?

options.text: Generates a naked carbanion via strong deprotonation
Oxidizes the aldehyde to a carboxylic acid
Acts as a dehydrating agent only without participating in C-C bond formation
Protonates the carbonyl oxygen of one molecule, increasing electrophilicity to accept the enol form of the second molecule

Aldol Condensation.explanation: In acid medium, carbonyl oxygen protonation enhances its electrophilic character, and the nucleophile is the neutral enol.

Aldol Condensation.question: Reaction of benzaldehyde with acetaldehyde in dilute $\text{NaOH}$ at room temperature gives predominantly:
Aldol Condensation.explanation: Ethanal forms the enolate which adds to benzaldehyde. Subsequent dehydration yields cinnamaldehyde (3-phenylprop-2-enal).

Aldol Condensation.question: Which of the following pairs can be distinguished by observing a precipitate after an Aldol Condensation followed by dehydration and $\text{I}_2/\text{NaOH}$ test?
Aldol Condensation.explanation: Ethanal gives crotonaldehyde (which retains a methyl ketone motif in other derivatives) or directly ethanal gives iodoform, whereas propanal does not.

Aldol Condensation.question: When excess formaldehyde is reacted with acetaldehyde in the presence of $\text{Ca(OH)}_2$, the final product formed via 3 aldol additions and 1 crossed Cannizzaro reaction is:
Aldol Condensation.explanation: Acetaldehyde has 3 $\alpha$-hydrogens, all of which undergo aldol addition with 3 molecules of formaldehyde to form $(\text{HOCH}_2)_3\text{C}-\text{CHO}$, which then undergoes crossed Cannizzaro with a 4th formaldehyde molecule to give pentaerythritol.

Aldol Condensation.question: In an aldol reaction, what is the effect of using a strong, sterically hindered base like Lithium Diisopropylamide (LDA) at $-78^\circ\text{C}$ on an unsymmetrical ketone like butan-2-one?

options.text: Directs thermodynamic deprotonation exclusively at the more substituted $\alpha$-carbon
Causes instant cleavage of the carbon-carbon carbonyl bond
Prevents any enolate formation due to steric shutdown
Directs kinetic deprotonation preferentially at the less hindered methyl $\alpha$-carbon

Aldol Condensation.explanation: Bulky LDA rapidly and irreversibly abstracts the more accessible proton from the less hindered methyl carbon at $-78^\circ\text{C}$ to form the kinetic enolate.

Aldol Condensation.question: The retro-aldol reaction is promoted by:

options.text: Heating $\beta$-hydroxy aldehydes or ketones with strong aqueous base
Exposure to ultraviolet light in argon atmosphere
Passing dry hydrogen gas over platinum catalyst

Aldol Condensation.explanation: Strong base deprotonates the $\beta$-hydroxyl group; expulsion of an enolate fragments the C-C bond in the reverse of the aldol addition.

Aldol Condensation.question: Which product is obtained from the crossed aldol condensation between benzaldehyde and propanal in the presence of dilute base?
Aldol Condensation.explanation: Propanal enolate ($-\text{CH(CH}_3)\text{CHO}$) attacks benzaldehyde, giving $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}=\text{C(CH}_3)\text{CHO}$ ($\alpha$-methylcinnamaldehyde).

Aldol Condensation.question: Why is formaldehyde the most reactive carbonyl electrophile in crossed aldol reactions?

options.text: It lacks electron-donating alkyl groups and has minimal steric crowding around the carbonyl carbon
It forms an exceptionally stable enolate anion

Aldol Condensation.explanation: With no alkyl groups to donate electron density or sterically shield the carbonyl, formaldehyde is the most electrophilic simple aldehyde.

Aldol Condensation.question: When cyclopentanone undergoes self-aldol condensation upon heating in dilute $\text{KOH}$, the product is:
Aldol Condensation.explanation: Self-aldol followed by dehydration gives the conjugated enone 2-cyclopentylidenecyclopentan-1-one.

Aldol Condensation.question: What happens when chloral ($\text{CCl}_3\text{CHO}$) is treated with dilute $\text{NaOH}$?

options.text: It undergoes haloform-type cleavage yielding chloroform and sodium formate instead of aldol
It oxidizes to trichloroacetic acid only
It forms a stable aromatic ring

Aldol Condensation.explanation: Chloral has no $\alpha$-hydrogens and the $\text{CCl}_3^-$ group is a very good leaving group; hydroxide attacks carbonyl to yield $\text{CHCl}_3$ and $\text{HCOONa}$.

Aldol Condensation.question: Which of the following compounds will undergo Aldol Condensation on treatment with dilute $\text{NaOH}$?
Aldol Condensation.explanation: Propanal has two $\alpha$-hydrogens, allowing enolate formation and self-aldol condensation; the other three aldehydes lack $\alpha$-hydrogens.

Aldol Condensation.question: What is the order of acidity of $\alpha$-hydrogens in carbonyl compounds responsible for enolate formation in aldol reactions?
Aldol Condensation.explanation: $\beta$-Dicarbonyls form enolates stabilized by two carbonyls ($\text{p}K_a \approx 9-11$), aldehydes ($\approx 17$), ketones ($\approx 20$), and esters ($\approx 25$).

Aldol Condensation.question: What is the intermediate formed during acid-catalyzed aldol condensation before attack on the protonated carbonyl?
Aldol Condensation.explanation: Under acidic conditions, tautomerization generates the nucleophilic neutral enol, which attacks the protonated carbonyl electrophile.

Aldol Condensation.question: In the crossed aldol condensation of benzaldehyde and acetone, why does acetone act as the nucleophile rather than benzaldehyde?

options.text: Acetone contains six accessible $\alpha$-hydrogens, whereas benzaldehyde contains zero $\alpha$-hydrogens
Benzaldehyde is more basic than acetone
Acetone carbonyl is less reactive than benzaldehyde carbonyl toward nucleophilic attack

Aldol Condensation.explanation: Benzaldehyde has no $\alpha$-hydrogens to lose as protons; only acetone can generate an enolate anion.

Aldol Condensation.question: Which of the following is the aldol addition product (before dehydration) of ethanal?
Aldol Condensation.explanation: Ethanal dimerizes to 3-hydroxybutanal: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CHO}$.

Aldol Condensation.question: The self-condensation of acetone in the presence of dry $\text{HCl}$ gas produces mesityl oxide and on further condensation yields:
Aldol Condensation.explanation: With dry $\text{HCl}$ gas, acetone condenses to mesityl oxide, which condenses with another molecule of acetone to yield phorone.

Aldol Condensation.question: Heating acetone with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ causes cyclic trimerization to give which aromatic hydrocarbon?
Aldol Condensation.explanation: Three molecules of acetone undergo acid-catalyzed condensation and cyclodehydration to yield 1,3,5-trimethylbenzene (mesitylene).

Aldol Condensation.question: Which of the following statements regarding the aldol condensation of butan-2-one is TRUE?

options.text: It can yield two different enolates, leading to regioisomeric aldol products
It cannot undergo aldol condensation because it is a ketone
It yields only a single unique condensation product
It undergoes exclusive Cannizzaro reaction instead

Aldol Condensation.explanation: Deprotonation can occur at C-1 (methyl) or C-3 (methylene), generating two isomeric enolates and resulting in regioisomers.

Aldol Condensation.question: When an aldehyde with $\alpha$-hydrogens is treated with $\text{D}_2\text{O}$ and catalytic $\text{NaOD}$, what happens rapidly?

options.text: The carbonyl carbon is replaced by deuterium
All $\alpha$-hydrogen atoms undergo rapid deuterium exchange via reversible enolate formation
The aldehyde undergoes instantaneous cleavage into methane
Deuterium adds exclusively across the $\text{C}=\text{O}$ double bond irreversibly

Aldol Condensation.explanation: Reversible deprotonation by $\text{OD}^-$ and reprotonation by $\text{D}_2\text{O}$ exchanges all acidic $\alpha$-hydrogens with deuterium.

Aldol Condensation.question: Identify the starting materials required to synthesize chalcone ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}=\text{CHCOC}_6\text{H}_5$) via aldol condensation:
Aldol Condensation.explanation: Chalcone is prepared by Claisen-Schmidt condensation between benzaldehyde and acetophenone in presence of base.

Aldol Condensation.question: The driving force for the dehydration of aldol addition products under mild conditions is:

options.text: Instability of all carbon-oxygen single bonds
Spontaneous formation of an aromatic sextet
Thermodynamic stabilization gained from the conjugated system $(\text{C}=\text{C}-\text{C}=\text{O})$

Aldol Condensation.explanation: Formation of an $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated carbonyl compound establishes extended orbital overlap (conjugation), lowering free energy.

Aldol Condensation.question: What is the product formed when 2-methylpropanal (isobutyraldehyde) is treated with dilute $\text{NaOH}$ at room temperature?
Aldol Condensation.explanation: Isobutyraldehyde has one $\alpha$-hydrogen: its enolate adds to another molecule to give the aldol 3-hydroxy-2,2,4-trimethylpentanal without dehydration (since product has no remaining $\alpha$-H).

Cannizzaro Reaction.question: Which of the following reaction conditions is characteristic of the Cannizzaro Reaction?

options.text: Concentrated aqueous alkali (50% $\text{NaOH}$ or $\text{KOH}$) with heating
Dilute aqueous alkali (1% $\text{NaOH}$) at room temperature

Cannizzaro Reaction.explanation: Cannizzaro reaction is a disproportionation reaction of aldehydes lacking $\alpha$-hydrogens, requiring concentrated base (50% $\text{NaOH}$ or $\text{KOH}$).

Cannizzaro Reaction.question: What structural feature is strictly REQUIRED for an aldehyde to undergo the Cannizzaro Reaction?

options.text: Presence of a secondary alcohol group
Presence of an ester functional group

Cannizzaro Reaction.explanation: Aldehydes with $\alpha$-hydrogens undergo rapid aldol condensation in base; only aldehydes lacking $\alpha$-hydrogens undergo Cannizzaro disproportionation.

Cannizzaro Reaction.question: Which of the following aldehydes undergoes the Cannizzaro Reaction when heated with 50% $\text{KOH}$?
Cannizzaro Reaction.explanation: Benzaldehyde lacks $\alpha$-hydrogens, so it undergoes Cannizzaro reaction to form benzyl alcohol and potassium benzoate.

Cannizzaro Reaction.question: What are the products formed when pure benzaldehyde is heated with 50% aqueous $\text{NaOH}$?
Cannizzaro Reaction.explanation: In the Cannizzaro reaction of benzaldehyde, one molecule is reduced to benzyl alcohol and the other is oxidized to sodium benzoate.

Cannizzaro Reaction.question: What is the rate-determining step (RDS) in the mechanism of the Cannizzaro Reaction?

options.text: Hydride ion ($\text{H}^-$) transfer from the tetrahedral anion intermediate to a second carbonyl molecule
Initial nucleophilic attack of hydroxide ion on the carbonyl carbon
Proton exchange between the carboxylate and alkoxide ions
Loss of water from the tetrahedral intermediate

Cannizzaro Reaction.explanation: Detailed kinetic studies show that the hydride transfer from the mono- or dianion to the neutral aldehyde carbonyl carbon is the slow, rate-determining step.

Cannizzaro Reaction.question: When benzaldehyde containing deuterium at the carbonyl carbon ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CDO}$) undergoes Cannizzaro reaction, the reaction exhibits a significant kinetic isotope effect ($k_\text{H} / k_\text{D} > 1$). This proves that:

options.text: Hydroxide attack is the rate-determining step
The carbon-hydrogen (or C-D) bond cleavage occurs during the rate-determining step
Proton transfer at the end is rate-determining
The reaction proceeds via a free-radical intermediate

Cannizzaro Reaction.explanation: A primary kinetic isotope effect indicates that the $\text{C}-\text{H}$ bond is broken during the rate-limiting hydride transfer step.

Cannizzaro Reaction.question: What happens in the Crossed Cannizzaro reaction between benzaldehyde and excess formaldehyde in concentrated $\text{NaOH}$?

options.text: Benzaldehyde is oxidized to sodium benzoate, and formaldehyde is reduced to methanol
Both aldehydes are converted into a cross-aldol condensation product
Formaldehyde is selectively oxidized to sodium formate, and benzaldehyde is reduced to benzyl alcohol
Benzaldehyde forms toluene and formaldehyde forms carbon dioxide

Cannizzaro Reaction.explanation: Formaldehyde is more electrophilic and forms the tetrahedral intermediate much faster; it transfers hydride to benzaldehyde, thus formaldehyde is oxidized to formate.

Cannizzaro Reaction.question: Which of the following aliphatic aldehydes undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction?
Cannizzaro Reaction.explanation: Trimethylacetaldehyde, $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{CHO}$, has a quaternary $\alpha$-carbon with zero $\alpha$-hydrogens, so it undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction.

Cannizzaro Reaction.question: What is the overall order of the Cannizzaro reaction with respect to aldehyde and base at very high base concentrations where the dianion is the reactive species?

options.text: Order 2 in aldehyde and Order 2 in base (Total order = 4)
Order 1 in aldehyde and Order 1 in base (Total order = 2)
Order 2 in aldehyde and Order 1 in base (Total order = 3)
Order 1 in aldehyde and Order 2 in base (Total order = 3)

Cannizzaro Reaction.explanation: At high base concentrations, two hydroxide ions deprotonate the hydrate to form a dianion; Rate = $k[\text{RCHO}]^2[\text{OH}^-]^2$, making the total reaction order 4.

Cannizzaro Reaction.question: What are the products formed from the disproportionation of formaldehyde ($\text{HCHO}$) in concentrated $\text{NaOH}$?
Cannizzaro Reaction.explanation: $2\text{HCHO} + \text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{OH} + \text{HCOONa}$. This is the classic self-Cannizzaro reaction of formaldehyde.

Cannizzaro Reaction.question: What is the product of the Intramolecular Cannizzaro reaction of glyoxal ($\text{OHC}-\text{CHO}$) in aqueous alkali?
Cannizzaro Reaction.explanation: Glyoxal undergoes intramolecular Cannizzaro reaction where one carbonyl group is oxidized and the other is reduced within the same molecule, giving glycolic acid (glycolate).

Cannizzaro Reaction.question: Treatment of phenylglyoxal ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COCHO}$) with aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ followed by acidification yields:
Cannizzaro Reaction.explanation: Phenylglyoxal undergoes intramolecular Cannizzaro rearrangement: hydride migrates from the aldehyde carbon to the ketone carbonyl carbon, yielding mandelic acid.

Cannizzaro Reaction.question: Why does chloral ($\text{CCl}_3\text{CHO}$) NOT undergo Cannizzaro reaction when treated with concentrated $\text{NaOH}$?

options.text: Because the trichloromethyl group ($\text{CCl}_3^-$) acts as a good leaving group, leading to haloform cleavage into chloroform and formate
Because it is an aromatic aldehyde
Because it forms a polymer instantly

Cannizzaro Reaction.explanation: Hydroxide attacks the carbonyl carbon of chloral, but instead of hydride transfer, the stable carbanion $\text{CCl}_3^-$ is expelled, giving chloroform and sodium formate.

Cannizzaro Reaction.question: Which of the following compounds gives a crossed Cannizzaro reaction with formaldehyde to form pentaerythritol?
Cannizzaro Reaction.explanation: Acetaldehyde reacts with 3 moles of $\text{HCHO}$ via aldol additions to form tris(hydroxymethyl)acetaldehyde, which then undergoes crossed Cannizzaro with a 4th $\text{HCHO}$ to give pentaerythritol.

Cannizzaro Reaction.question: In the Cannizzaro reaction of $p$-nitrobenzaldehyde vs $p$-methoxybenzaldehyde, which aldehyde forms the tetrahedral adduct with hydroxide faster?

options.text: Both react at exactly identical rates
$p$-Nitrobenzaldehyde, because the strongly electron-withdrawing $-\text{NO}_2$ group increases carbonyl electrophilicity
Neither can form a tetrahedral intermediate

Cannizzaro Reaction.explanation: Electron-withdrawing substituents like $-\text{NO}_2$ make the carbonyl carbon more electron-deficient, accelerating hydroxide attack.

Cannizzaro Reaction.question: Which of the following substituted benzaldehydes will undergo the Cannizzaro reaction at the slowest rate of hydride transfer?

options.text: $p$-Methoxybenzaldehyde (electron-donating $-\text{OCH}_3$ reduces hydride donor ability of intermediate)

Cannizzaro Reaction.explanation: Although electron donors make the carbonyl less electrophilic for initial attack, electron-rich anions are good hydride donors. Overall, $p$-methoxybenzaldehyde undergoes slower initial hydroxide attack.

Cannizzaro Reaction.question: When $o$-phthalaldehyde (benzene-1,2-dicarbaldehyde) is treated with concentrated $\text{KOH}$, what cyclic product is formed after acidification?
Cannizzaro Reaction.explanation: Intramolecular Cannizzaro converts one formyl group to $-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ and the other to $-\text{COOH}$; upon acidification, spontaneous lactonization yields phthalide.

Cannizzaro Reaction.question: When an equimolar mixture of benzaldehyde and $p$-methylbenzaldehyde undergoes crossed Cannizzaro reaction:

options.text: A mixture of all four possible redox products is formed with poor selectivity

Cannizzaro Reaction.explanation: Crossed Cannizzaro between two aromatic aldehydes of similar electrophilicity gives poor selectivity, yielding a mixture of both alcohols and both carboxylates.

Cannizzaro Reaction.question: Which reagent can reduce benzaldehyde to benzyl alcohol WITHOUT producing sodium benzoate as a byproduct (unlike Cannizzaro reaction)?
Cannizzaro Reaction.explanation: Hydride reducing agents like $\text{NaBH}_4$ or $\text{LiAlH}_4$ reduce aldehydes quantitatively to alcohols without disproportionation.

Cannizzaro Reaction.question: In the Cannizzaro reaction, the hydride ion is transferred directly from:

options.text: The alkali metal cation to the aldehyde
The tetrahedral intermediate to the carbonyl carbon of another aldehyde molecule via an intramolecular/intermolecular cyclic transition state

Cannizzaro Reaction.explanation: Hydride is transferred directly from the carbon of the negatively charged tetrahedral intermediate to the carbonyl carbon of a second aldehyde molecule.

Cannizzaro Reaction.question: Why is the Cannizzaro reaction classified as a disproportionation (dismutation) redox reaction?

options.text: The aldehyde acts simultaneously as both an oxidizing agent and a reducing agent
Only oxidation takes place while base is reduced
No oxidation or reduction occurs; it is an isomerization

Cannizzaro Reaction.explanation: One mole of aldehyde is oxidized to carboxylic acid while another mole is reduced to primary alcohol; thus the same reactant is both oxidized and reduced.

Cannizzaro Reaction.question: What is the effect of carrying out Cannizzaro reaction in heavy water ($\text{D}_2\text{O}$)?

options.text: The primary alcohol contains a $-\text{CD}_2\text{OH}$ group
The resulting primary alcohol contains NO carbon-bound deuterium ($-\text{CH}_2\text{OD}$), proving hydride transfer is direct from aldehyde carbon
The reaction does not proceed at all in heavy water

Cannizzaro Reaction.explanation: Direct transfer of hydride from the aldehyde carbon means no solvent proton/deuteron is incorporated onto the alcohol carbon atom; only the $-\text{OH}$ group exchanges to $-\text{OD}$.

Cannizzaro Reaction.question: Which of the following compounds will NOT give the Cannizzaro reaction?
Cannizzaro Reaction.explanation: Acetaldehyde contains 3 $\alpha$-hydrogens and undergoes rapid Aldol condensation rather than the Cannizzaro reaction.

Cannizzaro Reaction.question: What is the product when furfural (furan-2-carbaldehyde) is treated with 50% aqueous $\text{NaOH}$?
Cannizzaro Reaction.explanation: Furfural has no $\alpha$-hydrogens, so it undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction to yield furfuryl alcohol (reduction product) and sodium furoate (oxidation product).

Cannizzaro Reaction.question: In the crossed Cannizzaro reaction between $p$-chlorobenzaldehyde and formaldehyde in concentrated $\text{NaOH}$, the major alcohol formed is:
Cannizzaro Reaction.explanation: Formaldehyde is preferentially oxidized to sodium formate, reducing $p$-chlorobenzaldehyde to $p$-chlorobenzyl alcohol.

Cannizzaro Reaction.question: Which reaction intermediate is formed in the first step of the Cannizzaro reaction of benzaldehyde?
Cannizzaro Reaction.explanation: The hydroxide nucleophile attacks the carbonyl carbon to generate the tetrahedral monoanion $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH(OH)O}^-$.

Cannizzaro Reaction.question: What type of nucleophilic addition initiates the Cannizzaro reaction?

options.text: Nucleophilic attack of hydride on the carbonyl carbon
Electrophilic aromatic substitution on the benzene ring
Nucleophilic attack of $\text{OH}^-$ on the carbonyl carbon

Cannizzaro Reaction.explanation: The base $\text{OH}^-$ adds nucleophilically to the carbonyl carbon of the aldehyde lacking $\alpha$-hydrogens.

Cannizzaro Reaction.question: A mixture of 1 mole of benzaldehyde and 1 mole of formaldehyde was heated with 50% $\text{NaOH}$. The number of moles of benzyl alcohol formed will be approximately:
Cannizzaro Reaction.explanation: Formaldehyde is quantitatively oxidized to sodium formate, thereby reducing virtually all of the benzaldehyde (1 mole) into 1 mole of benzyl alcohol.

Cannizzaro Reaction.question: Which of the following undergoes an intramolecular Cannizzaro reaction?

options.text: Benzil (after hydroxide rearrangement to benzilic acid) / Phenylglyoxal

Cannizzaro Reaction.explanation: Phenylglyoxal ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COCHO}$) contains two adjacent carbonyl groups and undergoes intramolecular Cannizzaro to mandelic acid.

Cannizzaro Reaction.question: What is the role of hydroxide ion in Cannizzaro reaction at low base concentrations?

options.text: Acting as an oxidizing agent by accepting electrons
Acting as a nucleophile to generate the monoanionic tetrahedral intermediate
Acting as a solvent without reacting
Neutralizing carboxylic acid after the reaction is finished only

Cannizzaro Reaction.explanation: Hydroxide ion acts as a nucleophile, attacking the carbonyl carbon in the initial reversible step to form the tetrahedral monoanion.

Cannizzaro Reaction.question: Why is formaldehyde always the hydride donor in crossed Cannizzaro reactions with aromatic aldehydes?

options.text: Formaldehyde is less polar than aromatic aldehydes
Formaldehyde forms a stable aromatic resonance structure
Formaldehyde has higher electrophilicity toward $\text{OH}^-$, shifting the hydration/anion equilibrium far to the right, and its intermediate readily transfers hydride
Aromatic aldehydes do not react with $\text{OH}^-$ at all

Cannizzaro Reaction.explanation: Formaldehyde has no electron-donating groups and zero steric hindrance; it rapidly and quantitatively forms the tetrahedral anion that delivers hydride.

Cannizzaro Reaction.question: When cyclohexanecarbaldehyde is treated with concentrated $\text{NaOH}$:

options.text: It decomposes into cyclohexane and carbon monoxide
It undergoes Aldol condensation because it possesses one $\alpha$-hydrogen

Cannizzaro Reaction.explanation: Cyclohexanecarbaldehyde has one $\alpha$-hydrogen on C-1 of the ring, so it undergoes Aldol condensation, NOT Cannizzaro reaction.

Cannizzaro Reaction.question: What is the product when 2,2-dimethylbutanal is treated with 50% $\text{KOH}$?
Cannizzaro Reaction.explanation: 2,2-Dimethylbutanal lacks $\alpha$-hydrogens; thus it undergoes Cannizzaro reaction to yield the corresponding primary alcohol and carboxylate salt.

Cannizzaro Reaction.question: Cannizzaro reaction cannot be carried out on which of the following?
Cannizzaro Reaction.explanation: Acetaldehyde contains $\alpha$-hydrogens and will polymerize / undergo aldol condensation in concentrated base.

Cannizzaro Reaction.question: Which of the following tests can distinguish benzyl alcohol from benzoic acid (the two products of Cannizzaro reaction of benzaldehyde)?

options.text: Aqueous $\text{NaHCO}_3$ (gives brisk effervescence of $\text{CO}_2$ with benzoic acid only)

Cannizzaro Reaction.explanation: Benzoic acid is a carboxylic acid and reacts with $\text{NaHCO}_3$ to evolve $\text{CO}_2$ gas; benzyl alcohol is neutral and does not react.

Cannizzaro Reaction.question: Consider the reaction: $2\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CHO} \xrightarrow{\text{Al(OC}_2\text{H}_5)_3} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COOCH}_2\text{C}_6\text{H}_5$. This variant is known as:
Cannizzaro Reaction.explanation: The Tishchenko reaction is a variant of Cannizzaro reaction catalyzed by aluminium alkoxide (e.g., $\text{Al(OEt)}_3$) converting aldehydes into esters.

Cannizzaro Reaction.question: Which factor suppresses the Cannizzaro reaction in aldehydes possessing $\alpha$-hydrogens?

options.text: The rate of $\alpha$-deprotonation by base to form enolate is several orders of magnitude faster than nucleophilic attack of base to initiate hydride transfer
Hydride transfer is forbidden by orbital symmetry rules in aliphatic compounds
Base destroys the carbonyl bond in aliphatic aldehydes

Cannizzaro Reaction.explanation: Enolate formation (acid-base deprotonation) is extremely rapid, directing the reaction pathway towards aldol condensation rather than Cannizzaro.

Cannizzaro Reaction.question: In the Cannizzaro reaction of benzaldehyde, what is the fate of the nucleophilic hydroxide ion?

options.text: It is released back unchanged into the solution
Its oxygen atom becomes part of the carboxylate group of the oxidized product
Its hydrogen is transferred as a hydride ion
It reduces the aromatic ring to cyclohexadiene

Cannizzaro Reaction.explanation: Hydroxide attacks the carbonyl carbon; its oxygen is incorporated into the resulting carboxylic acid (benzoate anion).

Cannizzaro Reaction.question: Which of the following is an example of an intramolecular Cannizzaro reaction forming an $\alpha$-hydroxy carboxylic acid?

options.text: Benzil $\rightarrow$ Benzilic acid (Benzilic acid rearrangement) / Glyoxal $\rightarrow$ Glycolic acid

Cannizzaro Reaction.explanation: Glyoxal and phenylglyoxal undergo intramolecular Cannizzaro to form glycolic acid and mandelic acid respectively, which are $\alpha$-hydroxy carboxylic acids.

Cannizzaro Reaction.question: What is the effect of electron-donating groups (e.g. $-\text{CH}_3$, $-\text{OCH}_3$) on the rate of the Cannizzaro reaction of benzaldehyde?

options.text: They accelerate the reaction by tenfold
They cause rapid decomposition into benzene
They shift the reaction mechanism to free-radical polymerization
They decrease the overall reaction rate by diminishing the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon

Cannizzaro Reaction.explanation: Electron-donating groups reduce the positive charge on the carbonyl carbon, slowing down the initial nucleophilic addition of hydroxide.

Cannizzaro Reaction.question: Which isotope effect study conclusively proved that solvent protons are NOT involved in the hydride transfer step of the Cannizzaro reaction?

options.text: Carrying out the reaction in $\text{D}_2\text{O}$ yields alcohol with no C-D bond ($-\text{CH}_2\text{OD}$)
Carrying out the reaction in $^{18}\text{O}$-labeled water

Cannizzaro Reaction.explanation: If the hydride came from the solvent, the product would be $-\text{CHD-OH}$. Finding only $-\text{CH}_2\text{OD}$ proves the hydrogen is transferred directly from the aldehyde carbon.

Cannizzaro Reaction.question: What are the oxidation states of the carbonyl carbon in benzaldehyde, benzyl alcohol, and benzoic acid, respectively?

options.text: +2 in benzaldehyde, 0 in benzyl alcohol, +4 in benzoic acid
+1 in benzaldehyde, -1 in benzyl alcohol, +3 in benzoic acid
0 in benzaldehyde, -2 in benzyl alcohol, +2 in benzoic acid
+1 in benzaldehyde, +1 in benzyl alcohol, +1 in benzoic acid

Cannizzaro Reaction.explanation: Carbon in $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CHO}$ has oxidation state +1. In $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ it is -1, and in $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COOH}$ it is +3, confirming mutual oxidation and reduction.

Cannizzaro Reaction.question: Which of the following compounds gives benzyl alcohol when treated with concentrated $\text{NaOH}$?
Cannizzaro Reaction.explanation: Benzaldehyde undergoes Cannizzaro disproportionation in concentrated $\text{NaOH}$ to yield benzyl alcohol and sodium benzoate.

Cannizzaro Reaction.question: What is the product of heating a mixture of benzaldehyde and sodium formate with concentrated alkali?

options.text: Benzyl alcohol is formed as benzaldehyde is reduced while formate is oxidized to carbonate

Cannizzaro Reaction.explanation: Formate acts as a strong hydride donor under basic conditions, reducing benzaldehyde to benzyl alcohol while being oxidized to sodium carbonate.

Cannizzaro Reaction.question: In a classic JEE Main question: An unknown aldehyde $X$ ($\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$) gives a positive Cannizzaro reaction and does NOT reduce Tollens\' reagent differently from standard aldehydes. What is the structure of $X$?
Cannizzaro Reaction.explanation: Formula $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$ with no $\alpha$-hydrogens uniquely corresponds to 2,2-dimethylpropanal (pivalaldehyde).

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.question: What is the active electrophilic species in the Friedel-Crafts alkylation of benzene using an alkyl chloride and anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$?

options.text: A carbocation or a polarized alkyl chloride-Lewis acid complex ($\text{R}^\delta+\cdots\text{Cl}\cdots\text{Al}^\delta-\text{Cl}_3$)
A free alkyl radical formed by homolytic cleavage
A carbanion acting as a nucleophile
An acylium ion stabilized by resonance

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.explanation: Anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ acts as a Lewis acid and abstracts a chloride ion from the alkyl chloride to generate a carbocation or highly polarized complex that acts as the electrophile.

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.question: When benzene is treated with 1-chloropropane in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$, what is the major organic product?
Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.explanation: The primary propyl carbocation initially formed undergoes a 1,2-hydride shift to form the more stable secondary isopropyl carbocation, which then attacks the benzene ring to yield isopropylbenzene as the major product.

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.question: Which of the following aromatic substrates fails to undergo Friedel-Crafts alkylation with $\text{CH}_3\text{Cl} / \text{AlCl}_3$?
Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.explanation: Nitrobenzene is strongly deactivated by the $-\text{NO}_2$ group (strong $-M$ and $-I$ effects), making the benzene ring too electron-deficient to attack carbocations. Nitrobenzene is often used as a solvent for Friedel-Crafts reactions.

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.question: Aniline does not undergo Friedel-Crafts alkylation primarily because:

options.text: The amino group is an extremely strong meta-director
Aniline undergoes instantaneous $S_N2$ displacement at carbon
Aniline is completely insoluble in organic solvents
The basic amino group lone pair complexes with the Lewis acid catalyst $\text{AlCl}_3$, creating a strong positive charge that intensely deactivates the ring

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.explanation: The lone pair of electrons on the nitrogen atom in aniline acts as a Lewis base and coordinates with anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ to form $-\text{NH}_2^+-\text{AlCl}_3^-$. The positively charged nitrogen exerts a strong $-I$ effect and strongly deactivates the ring towards electrophilic attack.

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.question: What is a major synthetic limitation of Friedel-Crafts alkylation when attempting to prepare monoalkylbenzenes?

options.text: Polyalkylation readily occurs because the introduced alkyl group activates the aromatic ring toward further electrophilic attack
The reaction is irreversible and always yields tars
Alkyl halides completely polymerize under reaction conditions
The Lewis acid is consumed stoichiometrically without catalytic turnover

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.explanation: Because alkyl groups are electron-donating ($+I$ and hyperconjugation), the alkylated product is more reactive toward electrophilic substitution than the starting benzene, leading to significant polyalkylation (ortho/para dialkyl and trialkyl products).

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.question: Which of the following pairs cannot be used as an alkylating agent in a Friedel-Crafts alkylation reaction?
Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.explanation: Aryl and vinyl halides do not generate stable carbocations because $C_{sp^2}-Cl$ bonds have partial double bond character due to resonance and high $s$-character; thus chlorobenzene cannot act as an alkylating agent.

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.question: When benzene is treated with 2-chloro-2-methylpropane in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$, the product formed is:
Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.explanation: Ionization of 2-chloro-2-methylpropane by $\text{AlCl}_3$ directly gives the stable $3^\circ$ tert-butyl carbocation $(CH_3)_3C^+$, which attacks benzene to afford tert-butylbenzene.

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.question: When benzene reacts with isobutyl chloride (1-chloro-2-methylpropane) in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$, the major product is:
Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.explanation: The primary isobutyl carbocation undergoes an instantaneous 1,2-hydride shift to form the tertiary carbocation, $(CH_3)_3C^+$, leading exclusively to tert-butylbenzene as the major product.

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.question: Which reagent combination can be used to generate the isopropyl carbocation for alkylating benzene without using an alkyl halide?

options.text: Propene in the presence of concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ or $\text{HF}$
Propyne in the presence of Lindlar catalyst

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.explanation: Protonation of propene ($CH_3-CH=CH_2$) by a strong Brønsted acid ($H^+$) forms the more stable secondary carbocation $CH_3-\overset{+}{C}H-CH_3$, which readily alkylates benzene to form cumene.

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.question: What is the major product when benzene is treated with neopentyl chloride, $(CH_3)_3C-CH_2Cl$, in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$?
Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.explanation: The primary neopentyl carbocation $(CH_3)_3C-\overset{+}{C}H_2$ undergoes a 1,2-methyl shift to generate the more stable $3^\circ$ carbocation $CH_3-\overset{+}{C}(CH_3)-CH_2CH_3$ (tert-pentyl cation), which alkylates benzene to give 2-methyl-2-phenylbutane.

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.question: Which of the following Lewis acids is most commonly and strongly employed in Friedel-Crafts alkylations?
Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.explanation: Anhydrous aluminum chloride ($\text{AlCl}_3$) is a powerful electron-deficient Lewis acid that readily coordinates with halogen lone pairs to facilitate heterolytic $C-X$ bond cleavage.

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.question: When benzene reacts with 1-chlorobutane in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$, the major product is:
Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.explanation: The primary butyl carbocation undergoes a 1,2-hydride shift to generate the secondary butyl carbocation ($CH_3-\overset{+}{C}H-CH_2CH_3$), making sec-butylbenzene the predominant product over un-rearranged n-butylbenzene.

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.question: Intramolecular Friedel-Crafts alkylation of 4-phenylbutan-1-ol in concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ affords:
Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.explanation: Protonation and loss of water yields a carbocation that undergoes intramolecular electrophilic aromatic substitution to close a 6-membered ring, producing tetralin.

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.question: Why cannot straight-chain n-propylbenzene be prepared in high yield by direct Friedel-Crafts alkylation of benzene?

options.text: The primary propyl carbocation rapidly rearranges to the more stable secondary isopropyl carbocation via a 1,2-hydride shift
Benzene only reacts with methyl halides

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.explanation: Skeletal rearrangement of the primary carbocation to the secondary carbocation is kinetically faster than attack on the aromatic $\pi$-cloud, yielding cumene rather than n-propylbenzene.

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.question: How can n-propylbenzene be successfully synthesized from benzene without skeletal rearrangement?

options.text: Reacting benzene with propane and $\text{UV}$ light
Heating benzene with 1-chloropropane at $500^\circ\text{C}$ without catalyst
Friedel-Crafts acylation with propanoyl chloride / $\text{AlCl}_3$ followed by Clemmensen or Wolff-Kishner reduction

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.explanation: Acylation forms propiophenone via the non-rearranging acylium ion; subsequent reduction of the carbonyl group cleanly gives n-propylbenzene.

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.question: What happens when p-xylene is treated with methyl chloride and anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$?

options.text: No reaction occurs because p-xylene is deactivated

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.explanation: p-Xylene is activated by two methyl groups; substitution occurs at the vacant ortho position relative to one methyl group (meta to the other), giving 1,2,4-trimethylbenzene.

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.question: Under forcing conditions (excess $\text{AlCl}_3$ and heat), Friedel-Crafts alkylation is known to be reversible. This leads to thermodynamic equilibration favoring:

options.text: Meta-dialkylbenzenes (e.g., m-xylene over o- and p-xylene)
Complete dealkylation to pure benzene and gaseous alkane

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.explanation: Because alkylation is reversible, heating with Lewis acid enables isomerization via dealkylation/realkylation to the thermodynamically most stable, least sterically hindered isomer: meta-xylene.

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.question: Which of the following compounds undergoes Friedel-Crafts alkylation most rapidly?
Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.explanation: Methoxybenzene (anisole) possesses a strong $+M$ activating methoxy group which greatly enhances the nucleophilicity of the ortho and para positions of the aromatic ring.

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.question: Which of the following haloalkanes reacts fastest with benzene in the presence of $\text{AlCl}_3$?

options.text: All alkyl halides react at strictly identical rates

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.explanation: Because the Lewis acid $\text{AlCl}_3$ coordinates most strongly with the highly electronegative, hard base fluorine atom, alkyl fluorides generate polarized complexes and react fastest in Friedel-Crafts alkylation.

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.question: When 1,4-dichlorobutane is treated with benzene in the presence of excess $\text{AlCl}_3$, the cyclic product obtained is:
Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.explanation: Intermolecular alkylation followed by intramolecular alkylation on the same benzene ring yields the bicyclic hydrocarbon tetralin (1,2,3,4-tetrahydronaphthalene).

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.question: Which functional group on the benzene ring permits Friedel-Crafts alkylation without destroying the catalyst?
Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.explanation: Alkyl groups activate the ring moderately by $+I$ and hyperconjugation without Lewis-basic coordinating heteroatoms that deactivate the catalyst.

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.question: Treatment of benzene with excess methyl chloride and $\text{AlCl}_3$ leads eventually to which hexasubstituted benzene derivative?
Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.explanation: Because each methyl group introduced further activates the ring, exhaustive Friedel-Crafts methylation with excess methyl chloride leads to hexamethylbenzene.

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.question: What gas is evolved as a byproduct during Friedel-Crafts alkylation with an alkyl chloride?
Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.explanation: Loss of a proton from the arenium ion intermediate (Wheland complex) by reaction with $\text{AlCl}_4^-$ regenerates the aromatic sextet and yields $\text{HCl}$ gas and $\text{AlCl}_3$.

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.question: In the Friedel-Crafts alkylation of toluene with 2-chloropropane in the presence of $\text{AlCl}_3$, the major product isomer is:
Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.explanation: Toluene is ortho/para-directing; because the incoming isopropyl carbocation is relatively bulky, steric hindrance disfavors the ortho position, making p-cymene (4-isopropyltoluene) the major product.

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.question: Which of the following statements regarding the Arenium ion ($\sigma$-complex) in Friedel-Crafts alkylation is FALSE?

options.text: It is aromatic and has lower energy than benzene
It is non-aromatic because one ring carbon is $sp^3$-hybridized
Its positive charge is delocalized over the ortho and para positions relative to the $sp^3$ carbon
Its formation is generally the rate-determining step of the reaction

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.explanation: The arenium ion is non-aromatic (disrupted $\pi$-conjugation) and is a high-energy intermediate, not more stable than aromatic benzene.

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.question: When cyclohexyl chloride reacts with benzene in the presence of $\text{AlCl}_3$, what product is obtained?
Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.explanation: Ionization generates the secondary cyclohexyl carbocation, which directly attacks the benzene ring without skeletal rearrangement to form cyclohexylbenzene.

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.question: Friedel-Crafts alkylation of chlorobenzene with $\text{CH}_3\text{Cl} / \text{AlCl}_3$ yields predominantly:

options.text: Chlorobenzene does not react at all

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.explanation: Halogens are deactivating but ortho/para-directing due to resonance ($+M$) donation of unshared electron pairs. Steric factors favor the para product.

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.question: Which of the following catalysts cannot be used for Friedel-Crafts alkylation?
Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.explanation: $\text{NaOH}$ is a strong base and cannot act as a Lewis acid to abstract a halide ion; it would simply hydrolyze the alkyl halide.

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.question: Reaction of benzene with dichloromethane ($\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}_2$) in the presence of excess $\text{AlCl}_3$ yields:
Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.explanation: Benzyl chloride formed in the first step is even more reactive than dichloromethane and rapidly alkylates a second molecule of benzene to yield diphenylmethane.

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.question: Reaction of benzene with chloroform ($\text{CHCl}_3$) in the presence of $\text{AlCl}_3$ yields:
Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.explanation: Exhaustive stepwise electrophilic substitution of all three chlorine atoms by three benzene rings produces triphenylmethane ($(C_6H_5)_3CH$).

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.question: Reaction of benzene with carbon tetrachloride ($\text{CCl}_4$) in the presence of $\text{AlCl}_3$ stops primarily at:
Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.explanation: Due to extreme steric congestion around the central carbon atom, substitution of the fourth chlorine cannot occur; the reaction stops cleanly at triphenylmethyl chloride ($(C_6H_5)_3C-Cl$).

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.question: Why does Friedel-Crafts alkylation using 1-chloro-2,2-dimethylpropane (neopentyl chloride) not give neopentylbenzene?

options.text: Neopentyl chloride is an unreactive gas
The methyl groups are eliminated as methane
The neopentyl group decomposes to butadiene
The intermediate $1^\circ$ carbocation undergoes a fast 1,2-methyl shift to a tertiary carbocation

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.explanation: The primary neopentyl cation $(CH_3)_3C-\overset{+}{C}H_2$ experiences severe steric strain and rapidly undergoes a 1,2-methyl shift to form the tertiary 1,1-dimethylpropyl cation, yielding tert-pentylbenzene.

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.question: Which of the following solvents is best suited as an unreactive solvent for Friedel-Crafts alkylation?
Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.explanation: Nitrobenzene is deactivated and does not react under Friedel-Crafts conditions, and $\text{CS}_2$ has no aromatic ring or Lewis-basic coordinating atoms, making them excellent inert solvents.

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.question: The primary kinetic isotope effect ($k_H / k_D$) in the Friedel-Crafts alkylation of benzene with $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Cl}/\text{AlCl}_3$ is approximately:
Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.explanation: Because proton loss from the arenium ion ($\sigma$-complex) occurs after the rate-determining step (carbocation attack), breaking the $C-H$ bond is not rate-limiting, so $k_H/k_D \approx 1.0$.

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.question: Alkylation of benzene with 1-chlorobutane at lower temperatures versus higher temperatures gives:

options.text: More n-butylbenzene at lower temperatures and more sec-butylbenzene at higher temperatures

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.explanation: At lower temperatures, carbocation attack can partially compete with the 1,2-hydride shift before equilibrium is attained, yielding a higher proportion of unrearranged product.

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.question: Reaction of benzene with 2-chloropropane and $\text{AlCl}_3$ is an example of:
Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.explanation: The reaction proceeds via generation of an electrophile ($CH_3-\overset{+}{C}H-CH_3$), formation of a $\sigma$-complex (arenium ion), and deprotonation to retain aromaticity.

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.question: Which of the following haloalkanes can undergo Friedel-Crafts alkylation without any skeletal rearrangement of the alkyl group?
Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.explanation: Methyl and ethyl carbocations have no possible rearrangement pathways, so they alkylate benzene with 100% fidelity without skeletal rearrangement.

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.question: When naphthalene undergoes Friedel-Crafts alkylation with $\text{CH}_3\text{Cl} / \text{AlCl}_3$ at low temperature, the major product is:
Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.explanation: At low temperature (kinetic control), electrophilic attack occurs preferentially at the $\alpha$-position (position 1) because the corresponding arenium ion has two resonance contributors preserving an intact benzene sextet.

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.question: At higher temperature ($160^\circ\text{C}$), the Friedel-Crafts alkylation of naphthalene with methyl chloride yields:
Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.explanation: The $\beta$-isomer (position 2) is sterically less congested than the $\alpha$-isomer (which experiences peri-hydrogen interaction at C-8); thus thermodynamic control at high temperature favors 2-methylnaphthalene.

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.question: In the presence of Lewis acids, alkylbenzenes can undergo 'transalkylation'. When toluene is heated with catalytic $\text{AlCl}_3$ and $\text{HCl}$, it disproportionates into:
Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.explanation: Disproportionation (transalkylation) transfers a methyl group from one toluene molecule to another via protonation of the ring and dealkylation, generating benzene and dimethylbenzenes (xylenes).

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.question: Which of the following compounds can act as an alkylating agent in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$?
Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.explanation: Ethylene oxide coordinates with $\text{AlCl}_3$ to open the epoxide ring, generating a 2-haloethoxide or $\beta$-carbocation equivalent that alkylates benzene to form 2-phenylethanol.

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.question: Treatment of benzene with benzyl chloride in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ cleanly affords:
Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.explanation: Benzyl chloride readily generates the resonance-stabilized benzyl carbocation ($C_6H_5-\overset{+}{C}H_2$), which electrophilically substitutes benzene to give diphenylmethane.

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.question: Friedel-Crafts alkylation of benzene with $(R)\text{-2-chlorobutane}$ and $\text{AlCl}_3$ yields a product that is:
Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.explanation: The planar, achiral secondary sec-butyl carbocation ($CH_3-\overset{+}{C}H-CH_2CH_3$) formed as an intermediate is attacked with equal probability from top and bottom faces, resulting in complete racemization.

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.question: Which of the following pairs of reactants can undergo intramolecular Friedel-Crafts alkylation to yield indane?
Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.explanation: 3-Phenylpropyl chloride ($C_6H_5-CH_2-CH_2-CH_2-Cl$) upon treatment with $\text{AlCl}_3$ cyclizes via an intramolecular electrophilic attack to form the 5-membered ring of indane.

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.question: Why is anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ stored in tightly sealed bottles in the laboratory?

options.text: It rapidly fumes in moist air and hydrolyzes to $\text{Al(OH)}_3$ and $\text{HCl}$, losing its catalytic Lewis acidity
It turns into liquid metallic aluminum
It reacts violently with nitrogen gas in air

Friedel-Crafts Alkylation.explanation: Anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ is extremely hygroscopic. It reacts with atmospheric water moisture: $\text{AlCl}_3 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Al(OH)}_3 + 3\text{HCl}\uparrow$, which destroys the active Lewis acid.

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.question: What is the active electrophile in the Friedel-Crafts acylation of benzene with acetyl chloride and anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$?
Friedel-Crafts Acylation.explanation: Reaction of acetyl chloride with $\text{AlCl}_3$ produces the linear, resonance-stabilized acylium ion in which all atoms have a complete octet of valence electrons.

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.question: Friedel-Crafts acylation does NOT suffer from polyacylation because:

options.text: The acyl chloride decomposes completely after one turnover
The introduced acyl group is strongly electron-withdrawing ($-M$ and $-I$), significantly deactivating the product ring toward further electrophilic attack
The product ketone is volatile and escapes the reaction vessel
The catalyst $\text{AlCl}_3$ is destroyed by the starting material

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.explanation: The carbonyl group of the aryl ketone withdraws electron density from the ring by resonance ($-M$), making the product far less reactive than the initial aromatic hydrocarbon.

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.question: How much anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ catalyst is required for the Friedel-Crafts acylation using an acyl chloride?

options.text: A minute catalytic amount (0.01 molar equivalent)
Slightly more than 1.0 molar equivalent (stoichiometric amount)
Friedel-Crafts acylation does not require any $\text{AlCl}_3$

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.explanation: Because the basic carbonyl oxygen of the ketone product complexes strongly with the Lewis acid $\text{AlCl}_3$ to form a stable 1:1 complex, at least 1 full equivalent of $\text{AlCl}_3$ is bound and must be used.

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.question: How much anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ is required when an acid anhydride (e.g., acetic anhydride) is used as the acylating agent?
Friedel-Crafts Acylation.explanation: An acid anhydride produces one mole of ketone and one mole of carboxylic acid byproduct, both of which complex strongly with $\text{AlCl}_3$; hence more than 2 molar equivalents of Lewis acid are required.

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.question: What is the major organic product formed when benzene reacts with acetyl chloride in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$?
Friedel-Crafts Acylation.explanation: Acetyl chloride ($CH_3COCl$) introduces an acetyl group ($-COCH_3$) onto the benzene ring to yield acetophenone and $HCl$.

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.question: What is the product when benzene reacts with benzoyl chloride in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$?
Friedel-Crafts Acylation.explanation: Electrophilic attack of the benzoylium ion ($C_6H_5-C\equiv O^+$) on benzene forms diphenylmethanone (benzophenone).

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.question: Unlike Friedel-Crafts alkylation, Friedel-Crafts acylation proceeds WITHOUT carbocation rearrangement because:

options.text: Acyl halides do not form ionic intermediates
The reaction is carried out at absolute zero
The resonance-stabilized acylium ion does not undergo skeletal rearrangement
The acyl group is too small to rearrange

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.explanation: The acylium ion ($R-C\equiv O^+$) is exceptionally stable due to complete octets on both carbon and oxygen, so it undergoes direct substitution without 1,2-hydride or alkyl shifts.

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.question: What sequence of reactions is used to synthesize pure n-butylbenzene from benzene in high yield?

options.text: Reaction of benzene with butane gas under pressure
Friedel-Crafts acylation with butanoyl chloride / $\text{AlCl}_3$ followed by Clemmensen reduction ($\text{Zn-Hg} / \text{HCl}$)

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.explanation: Acylation with butanoyl chloride introduces the unbranched 4-carbon acyl chain without rearrangement; subsequent Clemmensen reduction reduces the carbonyl $>C=O$ to methylene $-CH_2-$.

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.question: When benzene is treated with phthalic anhydride in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$, followed by heating with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, the product obtained is:
Friedel-Crafts Acylation.explanation: The initial acylation yields o-benzoylbenzoic acid; subsequent intramolecular electrophilic acylation (cyclodehydration) with concentrated $H_2SO_4$ produces 9,10-anthraquinone.

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.question: When benzene is treated with succinic anhydride in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$, what intermediate is formed?
Friedel-Crafts Acylation.explanation: Ring opening of succinic anhydride by electrophilic attack on benzene produces 4-oxo-4-phenylbutanoic acid, the first step of the Haworth synthesis.

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.question: Haworth synthesis of naphthalene involves which sequence starting from benzene?

options.text: Direct alkylation with 1,4-dichlorobutane followed by oxidation

Acylation with succinic anhydride $\rightarrow$ Clemmensen reduction $\rightarrow$ Cyclization with $\text{polyphosphoric acid} / \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ $\rightarrow$ Clemmensen reduction $\rightarrow$ Dehydrogenation with $\text{Se} / \text{Pd}$
Wurtz coupling of two molecules of benzyl chloride

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.explanation: The Haworth synthesis utilizes succinic anhydride to build the second 6-membered ring onto benzene through sequential acylation, reduction, cyclization, reduction, and aromatization.

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.question: Intramolecular Friedel-Crafts acylation of 4-phenylbutanoyl chloride in the presence of $\text{AlCl}_3$ gives:
Friedel-Crafts Acylation.explanation: The acylium ion formed at the terminus of the 4-carbon chain attacks the ortho position of the phenyl ring to close a 6-membered cyclic ketone, forming $\alpha$-tetralone.

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.question: Intramolecular Friedel-Crafts acylation of 3-phenylpropanoyl chloride in the presence of $\text{AlCl}_3$ gives:
Friedel-Crafts Acylation.explanation: Electrophilic attack of the terminal acylium ion on the benzene ring closes a 5-membered cyclic ring, producing 1-indanone.

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.question: Which of the following compounds CANNOT be prepared by direct Friedel-Crafts acylation of benzene?
Friedel-Crafts Acylation.explanation: Formyl chloride ($HCOCl$) is unstable at room temperature and decomposes into $CO$ and $HCl$; therefore, benzaldehyde cannot be prepared by standard Friedel-Crafts acylation (Gattermann-Koch reaction is used instead).

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.question: Gattermann-Koch reaction circumvents the instability of formyl chloride by generating it in situ from:

options.text: Formic acid and thionyl chloride at high temperature
Carbon monoxide ($\text{CO}$) and hydrogen chloride ($\text{HCl}$) in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ and $\text{CuCl}$

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.explanation: Passing $CO$ and $HCl$ gas into benzene in the presence of $AlCl_3/CuCl$ generates the formyl cation $[H-C\equiv O]^+$ in situ, yielding benzaldehyde in good yield.

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.question: Why must the product of a Friedel-Crafts acylation be treated with aqueous acid during workup?

options.text: To hydrolyze the ketone-$\text{AlCl}_3$ Lewis acid-base complex and release the free ketone

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.explanation: The ketone product forms a strong adduct with $\text{AlCl}_3$ via its carbonyl oxygen: $Ar-CO(R)\cdot AlCl_3$. Aqueous acid hydrolysis breaks this complex, precipitating aluminum salts and liberating the organic ketone.

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.question: When toluene undergoes Friedel-Crafts acylation with acetyl chloride and $\text{AlCl}_3$, what is the major product?
Friedel-Crafts Acylation.explanation: Methyl is ortho/para-directing; because the incoming acyl group ($CH_3C\equiv O^+$) is relatively large and coordinates with $AlCl_3$, steric hindrance strongly disfavors the ortho position, giving the para product in $>90\%$ yield.

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.question: Which of the following aromatic substrates fails to undergo Friedel-Crafts acylation?
Friedel-Crafts Acylation.explanation: Nitrobenzene is strongly deactivated by the $-\text{NO}_2$ group ($-M, -I$) and does not react; it is completely inert to acylation.

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.question: Phenols undergo Friedel-Crafts acylation with acyl chlorides to give phenyl esters (O-acylation). When this phenyl ester is heated with anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$, it rearranges to ortho- and para-hydroxyketones via the:
Friedel-Crafts Acylation.explanation: The Fries rearrangement involves heating a phenolic ester with Lewis acid $\text{AlCl}_3$ to achieve acyl migration from the phenolic oxygen to the ortho and para ring carbons.

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.question: In the Fries rearrangement of phenyl acetate, lower temperatures ($<100^\circ\text{C}$) favor which isomer?
Friedel-Crafts Acylation.explanation: At lower temperatures, the kinetically controlled product (para-hydroxyacetophenone) predominates, whereas higher temperatures ($>140^\circ\text{C}$) favor the thermodynamically stable ortho isomer due to intramolecular hydrogen bonding.

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.question: Reaction of anisole (methoxybenzene) with acetyl chloride in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ yields predominantly:
Friedel-Crafts Acylation.explanation: The methoxy group is a strong $+M$ ortho/para-director. Steric hindrance at the ortho position directs the bulky acylium ion predominantly to the para position.

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.question: Which of the following compounds gives a negative result in Friedel-Crafts acylation?
Friedel-Crafts Acylation.explanation: The cyano group is strongly electron-withdrawing by both resonance ($-M$) and inductive ($-I$) effects, deactivating the ring toward electrophilic attack.

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.question: Friedel-Crafts acylation of chlorobenzene with acetyl chloride and $\text{AlCl}_3$ yields:
Friedel-Crafts Acylation.explanation: Chlorine is ortho/para-directing due to its $+M$ resonance effect; steric crowding favors substitution at the 4-position (para).

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.question: What is the function of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ in Friedel-Crafts acylation?

options.text: It oxidizes the acyl chloride to a carboxylic acid
It acts as a Brønsted base to remove protons from benzene
It serves as a phase-transfer catalyst
It acts as a Lewis acid to abstract chloride ion from the acyl halide to generate an acylium ion

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.explanation: $\text{AlCl}_3$ coordinates with the chlorine atom of $RCOCl$ to induce heterolytic cleavage of the $C-Cl$ bond, generating $R-C\equiv O^+$ and $AlCl_4^-$.

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.question: Acylation of ferrocene with acetic anhydride in the presence of $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ yields acetylferrocene. This proves that:

options.text: Ferrocene is super-aromatic and far more reactive than benzene toward electrophiles

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.explanation: Ferrocene reacts smoothly with mild Lewis acids like $H_3PO_4$ instead of harsh $AlCl_3$, demonstrating that the cyclopentadienyl rings in ferrocene are significantly more electron-rich than benzene.

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.question: In Friedel-Crafts acylation of benzene, what is the hybridization of the carbonyl carbon in the acylium ion ($R-C\equiv O^+$)?
Friedel-Crafts Acylation.explanation: The acylium ion has a linear structure with a carbon-oxygen triple bond ($R-C\equiv O^+$), where the central carbonyl carbon is $sp$-hybridized with a bond angle of $180^\circ$.

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.question: When ethyl chloroformate ($\text{Cl}-\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_3$) reacts with benzene in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$, the product is:
Friedel-Crafts Acylation.explanation: Ethyl chloroformate acts as an acyl chloride derivative; loss of chloride generates the ethoxycarbonyl cation $[EtO-C\equiv O]^+$, which attacks benzene to form ethyl benzoate.

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.question: When phosgene ($\text{COCl}_2$) is treated with excess benzene in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$, what is the final product?
Friedel-Crafts Acylation.explanation: Both chlorine atoms in phosgene are sequentially replaced by phenyl groups in two successive Friedel-Crafts acylations, yielding benzophenone.

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.question: When oxalyl chloride ($(\text{COCl})_2$) reacts with excess benzene in the presence of $\text{AlCl}_3$, the major product is:
Friedel-Crafts Acylation.explanation: Both acyl chloride termini of oxalyl chloride undergo electrophilic substitution on separate benzene rings to afford the $\alpha$-diketone benzil ($C_6H_5-CO-CO-C_6H_5$).

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.question: Which of the following acyl halides reacts most readily in Friedel-Crafts acylation?
Friedel-Crafts Acylation.explanation: Due to the high affinity of the hard Lewis acid $\text{AlCl}_3$ for the hard base fluorine, acyl fluorides coordinate strongly and react fastest in Friedel-Crafts acylation.

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.question: What is the product when thiophene undergoes Friedel-Crafts acylation with acetyl chloride and $\text{SnCl}_4$?
Friedel-Crafts Acylation.explanation: Thiophene is an electron-rich heteroaromatic ring that undergoes electrophilic substitution preferentially at the 2-position ($\alpha$-position) under mild conditions.

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.question: Why is a weaker Lewis acid such as $\text{SnCl}_4$ or $\text{ZnCl}_2$ preferred over $\text{AlCl}_3$ for the acylation of furan or thiophene?

options.text: Furan does not react with acyl chlorides
Furan and thiophene are acid-sensitive and polymerize readily in the presence of strong Lewis acids like $\text{AlCl}_3$

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.explanation: Furan and thiophene have high electron density and tend to resinify/polymerize in the presence of vigorous Lewis acids; milder catalysts prevent ring cleavage.

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.question: Treatment of benzene with acetic anhydride in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ yields:
Friedel-Crafts Acylation.explanation: Cleavage of acetic anhydride by $\text{AlCl}_3$ yields the acetylium ion and an acetate-aluminum complex; substitution on benzene forms acetophenone with acetic acid as the byproduct.

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.question: Which reagent combination converts acetophenone directly into ethylbenzene?
Friedel-Crafts Acylation.explanation: Clemmensen or Wolff-Kishner reduction completely reduces the benzylic carbonyl group of an aromatic ketone to a methylene group ($-CH_2-$).

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.question: Why is Friedel-Crafts acylation preferred over alkylation for synthesizing alkylbenzenes?

options.text: It does not require any Lewis acid catalyst
It can be carried out using water as solvent
It avoids both carbocation rearrangement and polyalkylation
It converts benzene into benzoic acid directly

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.explanation: Acylation cleanly introduces the carbon skeleton without rearrangements (linear acylium ion) and deactivates the ring against polyacylation; subsequent reduction provides pure linear alkylbenzenes.

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.question: Which of the following statements regarding the Clemmensen reduction of acetophenone is TRUE?

options.text: It uses hydrazine and basic glycol
It selectively reduces aromatic rings to cyclohexanes
It uses amalgamated zinc and concentrated hydrochloric acid to reduce $>\text{C}=\text{O}$ to $-\text{CH}_2-$

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.explanation: Clemmensen reduction specifically uses $Zn(Hg)$ and concentrated $HCl$ to reduce aldehydes and ketones to hydrocarbons.

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.question: What is the product when biphenyl is treated with acetyl chloride and $\text{AlCl}_3$?
Friedel-Crafts Acylation.explanation: The phenyl substituent on the first ring is an ortho/para-director ($+M$). Steric hindrance at the ortho position directs monoacylation exclusively to the para (4) position.

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.question: Acylation of naphthalene with acetyl chloride and $\text{AlCl}_3$ in carbon disulfide ($\text{CS}_2$) solvent at $0^\circ\text{C}$ gives:
Friedel-Crafts Acylation.explanation: In non-polar solvents like $CS_2$ at low temperature, kinetic control dominates, directing the acyl group to the more nucleophilic $\alpha$-position (position 1).

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.question: Acylation of naphthalene with acetyl chloride and $\text{AlCl}_3$ in nitrobenzene solvent at room temperature gives:

options.text: Naphthalene does not react in nitrobenzene

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.explanation: In bulky coordinating solvents like nitrobenzene, the effective size of the acylating complex increases, favoring attack at the sterically unhindered $\beta$-position (position 2).

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.question: Which of the following compounds will NOT form an acylium ion upon treatment with anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$?
Friedel-Crafts Acylation.explanation: Ethyl chloride is an alkyl halide, not an acyl halide; it generates an ethyl cation (or polarized complex), not an acylium ion.

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.question: Which gas is liberated when an acyl chloride reacts with benzene in the presence of $\text{AlCl}_3$?
Friedel-Crafts Acylation.explanation: Loss of a proton from the Wheland intermediate regenerates the aromatic sextet while forming $HCl$ gas: $ArH + RCOCl \rightarrow ArCOR + HCl$.

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.question: When benzene is acylated with chloroacetyl chloride ($\text{ClCH}_2\text{COCl}$) and $\text{AlCl}_3$, which bond cleaves to form the electrophile?

options.text: The acyl chloride $\text{C}-\text{Cl}$ bond, forming the $\text{ClCH}_2-\overset{+}{\text{C}}=\text{O}$ ion

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.explanation: The acyl chlorine is far more reactive toward Lewis acid abstraction than the alkyl chlorine, forming the chloromethyl acylium ion which yields 2-chloroacetophenone (phenacyl chloride).

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.question: What is the common name of phenacyl chloride ($C_6H_5-CO-CH_2Cl$), prepared by Friedel-Crafts acylation of benzene with chloroacetyl chloride?

options.text: Tear gas (riot control agent / CN gas)

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.explanation: Phenacyl chloride is a potent lachrymator commonly employed as tear gas (designated CN) in riot control.

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.question: Can benzoic acid be converted directly to benzophenone by treatment with benzene and $\text{AlCl}_3$?

options.text: Yes, in quantitative yield at room temperature
Yes, with elimination of oxygen gas
Yes, but only under UV irradiation
No, carboxylic acids react poorly because they coordinate with $\text{AlCl}_3$ and are poor electrophiles compared to acyl halides

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.explanation: Carboxylic acids do not form acylium ions readily with $\text{AlCl}_3$; they must first be converted into acyl chlorides using $SOCl_2$ or $PCl_5$ before Friedel-Crafts acylation.

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.question: What is the role of adding excess ice/water after completion of a Friedel-Crafts acylation?

options.text: It decomposes the $\text{ketone}\cdot\text{AlCl}_3$ complex and dissolves the hydrated aluminum salts into the aqueous layer
It hydrolyzes the ketone to a carboxylic acid

Friedel-Crafts Acylation.explanation: The workup step decomposes the stable ketone-Lewis acid complex, hydrolyzing aluminum chloride into water-soluble basic aluminum salts ($Al(OH)_3 / AlCl_3\cdot 6H_2O$) and releasing the free ketone into the organic phase.

Reimer-Tiemann Reaction.question: What are the reagents used in the standard Reimer-Tiemann Reaction to synthesize salicylaldehyde from phenol?

options.text: Chloroform ($\text{CHCl}_3$) and aqueous sodium hydroxide ($\text{NaOH}$) at $340\text{ K}$, followed by acid hydrolysis
Formic acid and concentrated sulfuric acid

Reimer-Tiemann Reaction.explanation: Phenol is treated with chloroform ($\text{CHCl}_3$) in the presence of aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ at $\approx 60-70^\circ\text{C}$ ($340\text{ K}$) followed by acidification to yield salicylaldehyde.

Reimer-Tiemann Reaction.question: What is the electrophile in the Reimer-Tiemann reaction of phenol with chloroform and $\text{NaOH}$?
Reimer-Tiemann Reaction.explanation: Hydroxide abstracts a proton from chloroform followed by $\alpha$-elimination of chloride ion to generate neutral, electron-deficient dichlorocarbene (:\!\text{CCl}_2) with a vacant p orbital.

Reimer-Tiemann Reaction.question: How is the electrophile dichlorocarbene (:\!\text{CCl}_2) generated in situ in the Reimer-Tiemann reaction?

options.text: Via homolytic cleavage of carbon-chlorine bond by UV light

Via $\alpha$-elimination of $\text{HCl}$ from chloroform by strong base: $\text{CHCl}_3 + \text{OH}^- \rightleftharpoons :\!\text{CCl}_3^- + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow :\!\text{CCl}_2 + \text{Cl}^-$
Via reductive elimination from mercuric chloride

Reimer-Tiemann Reaction.explanation: Deprotonation of $\text{CHCl}_3$ yields the trichloromethanide anion, which loses a chloride ion ($\alpha$-elimination) to produce dichlorocarbene.

Reimer-Tiemann Reaction.question: What is the major organic product formed when phenol undergoes Reimer-Tiemann reaction with $\text{CHCl}_3 / \text{NaOH}$?
Reimer-Tiemann Reaction.explanation: Salicylaldehyde (ortho-isomer) is the major product due to favorable six-membered cyclic chelation and intramolecular hydrogen bonding in the intermediate phenoxide-sodium complex.

Reimer-Tiemann Reaction.question: What product is formed when phenol is treated with carbon tetrachloride ($\text{CCl}_4$) and aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ (modified Reimer-Tiemann)?
