Gattermann Reaction.explanation: Copper metal donates a single electron to the diazonium ion ($	ext{ArN}_2^+ + Cu ightarrow 	ext{ArN}_2^ ullet + Cu^+$), which expels $N_2$ to generate an aryl radical ($	ext{Ar}^ ullet$). Halide abstraction from the acid/copper complex yields the haloarene.

Gattermann Reaction.question: What byproduct biaryl can be formed in minor amounts during the Gattermann reaction via radical dimerization?
Gattermann Reaction.explanation: Dimerization of two aryl radicals ($2	ext{Ar}^ ullet ightarrow 	ext{Ar}-	ext{Ar}$) on the copper surface produces traces of biphenyl as a side product.

Gattermann Reaction.question: Can iodobenzene be prepared by the Gattermann reaction?

options.text: It is unnecessary because benzenediazonium chloride reacts with aqueous $\text{KI}$ smoothly without any copper catalyst
Yes, it is the only way to synthesize iodobenzene
No, iodobenzene cannot be made from diazonium salts
Yes, using copper powder and dry iodine gas

Gattermann Reaction.explanation: Aryl iodides do not require copper catalysts; simply warming the diazonium salt solution with potassium iodide ($KI$) gives iodobenzene in high yield.

Gattermann Reaction.question: Can fluorobenzene be prepared by the Gattermann reaction?

options.text: Yes, using copper powder and aqueous $\text{HF}$
No, fluorobenzene is prepared by the Balz-Schiemann reaction (thermal decomposition of $\text{ArN}_2^+\text{BF}_4^-$)
Yes, using copper powder and fluorine gas
Yes, fluorobenzene is the main product with $HBF_4$ at $0^\circ\text{C}$

Gattermann Reaction.explanation: Aqueous $HF$ cannot be used with copper powder; fluorobenzene is prepared via the Balz-Schiemann reaction by precipitating the insoluble diazonium fluoroborate and dry-heating it.

Gattermann Reaction.question: How does the 'Gattermann Reaction' differ from the 'Gattermann-Koch Reaction'?

options.text: They are completely identical reactions discovered in different years
Gattermann reaction makes carboxylic acids; Gattermann-Koch makes ketones
Gattermann reaction converts diazonium salts to haloarenes using $\text{Cu/HX}$, while Gattermann-Koch formylates benzene to benzaldehyde using $\text{CO} + \text{HCl} / \text{AlCl}_3 / \text{CuCl}$
Gattermann-Koch uses nitric acid on toluene

Gattermann Reaction.explanation: The Gattermann reaction replaces $-N_2^+$ with halogen using $Cu/HX$. The Gattermann-Koch reaction is an electrophilic formylation of arenes using $CO + HCl$ catalyzed by $AlCl_3/CuCl$ to produce benzaldehyde.

Gattermann Reaction.question: How does the 'Gattermann Aldehyde Synthesis' differ from the Gattermann-Koch reaction?

options.text: Gattermann aldehyde synthesis uses formaldehyde and base
Gattermann aldehyde synthesis uses chloroform and alkali
Gattermann aldehyde synthesis uses hydrogen cyanide ($\text{HCN}$) and $\text{HCl}$ with $\text{AlCl}_3$ or $\text{ZnCl}_2$, making it applicable to activated phenols and heterocyclic compounds

Gattermann Reaction.explanation: Gattermann aldehyde synthesis uses $HCN + HCl$ (or $Zn(CN)_2 + HCl$) to introduce a formyl group into electron-rich phenols and heterocyclic compounds where Gattermann-Koch fails.

Gattermann Reaction.question: Why is freshly prepared copper powder preferred over old oxidized copper turnings in the Gattermann reaction?

options.text: Freshly precipitated copper has a high surface area and is free from passivating copper oxide films, facilitating electron transfer
Old copper contains toxic zinc impurities
Oxidized copper absorbs all the diazonium salt
Copper turnings dissolve in water instantly

Gattermann Reaction.explanation: Freshly prepared copper powder (often made by reducing copper sulfate solution with zinc dust) has very small particle size, high surface area, and active metallic sites free of oxide coating.

Gattermann Reaction.question: What happens if the temperature of the arenediazonium chloride solution exceeds $5^\circ\text{C}$ before the Gattermann reaction?

options.text: The diazonium salt turns into benzene
The diazonium salt hydrolyzes with water to form phenol with evolution of nitrogen
The diazonium salt explodes violently into chlorine gas
The solution freezes into an inert gel

Gattermann Reaction.explanation: Arenediazonium salts are thermally unstable in aqueous solution above $5^\circ C$ ($278	ext{ K}$) and undergo nucleophilic attack by water: $	ext{ArN}_2^+ + H_2O ightarrow 	ext{ArOH} + N_2 + H^+$.

Gattermann Reaction.question: Starting from p-toluidine, which sequence yields p-chlorotoluene via the Gattermann reaction?

options.text: Direct reaction of p-toluidine with chlorine gas in sunlight
Diazotization with $\text{NaNO}_2 / \text{HCl}$ at $0-5^\circ\text{C}$ followed by treatment with $\text{Cu}$ powder and concentrated $\text{HCl}$

Gattermann Reaction.explanation: Diazotization of the primary aromatic amino group gives 4-methylbenzenediazonium chloride; subsequent treatment with $Cu$ powder and concentrated $HCl$ cleanly affords p-chlorotoluene.

Gattermann Reaction.question: What is the formal role of copper powder in the Gattermann reaction?
Gattermann Reaction.explanation: Copper acts as a heterogeneous catalyst, transiently oxidized to $Cu(I)$ during single electron transfer to the diazonium cation and regenerated during the catalytic cycle.

Gattermann Reaction.question: When o-nitroaniline is diazotized and treated with $\text{Cu}$ powder and concentrated $\text{HCl}$, what is the product?
Gattermann Reaction.explanation: The diazonium group at the 1-position is replaced by chlorine under Gattermann conditions, leaving the 2-nitro group intact to give 1-chloro-2-nitrobenzene.

Gattermann Reaction.question: Why is Gattermann reaction performed in strongly acidic medium?

options.text: To keep the copper powder from dissolving
To provide a high concentration of halide counterions and prevent coupling of diazonium ions with unreacted amine to form diazoamino compounds
Because diazonium salts only dissolve in pure acid

Gattermann Reaction.explanation: Excess acid keeps the unreacted aromatic amine completely protonated as an anilinium ion, preventing it from acting as a nucleophile to couple with diazonium ions to form triazenes (diazoamino compounds).

Gattermann Reaction.question: Which of the following compounds CANNOT be prepared directly from benzenediazonium chloride using the Gattermann reaction with $\text{Cu}$ powder?
Gattermann Reaction.explanation: Fluorobenzene cannot be synthesized with copper powder and $HF$; it requires the Balz-Schiemann thermal decomposition of the diazonium tetrafluoroborate salt.

Gattermann Reaction.question: In the Gattermann reaction, what is the fate of the nitrogen atoms originally present in the $-\text{N}_2^+$ group?

options.text: They remain attached to copper as copper nitride
They are converted into ammonium chloride
They are released as inert, diatomic nitrogen gas ($\text{N}_2$) into the atmosphere

Gattermann Reaction.explanation: The $C-N$ bond breaks homolytically, releasing molecular $N_2$ gas: $	ext{Ar}-N_2^+ + e^- ightarrow 	ext{Ar}^ ullet + N_2\uparrow$.

Gattermann Reaction.question: Who was the German chemist who discovered both the Gattermann reaction and the Gattermann-Koch reaction?
Gattermann Reaction.explanation: Ludwig Gattermann (1860–1920) discovered the copper-catalyzed replacement of diazonium groups (1890) as well as the Gattermann-Koch formylation of aromatic compounds.

Gattermann Reaction.question: What happens when benzenediazonium chloride is treated with copper powder in the presence of potassium cyanide and $\text{HCN}$?

options.text: Benzonitrile ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CN}$) is formed with evolution of $\text{N}_2$

Gattermann Reaction.explanation: Under Gattermann conditions with cyanide, the diazonium group is replaced by the cyano group ($-CN$) to produce benzonitrile.

Gattermann Reaction.question: What is the state of hybridization of the aromatic carbon bearing the diazonium group before and after the Gattermann reaction?
Gattermann Reaction.explanation: The aromatic carbon is part of the planar benzene ring in both the reactant (benzenediazonium cation) and product (chlorobenzene) and remains $sp^2$-hybridized throughout.

Gattermann Reaction.question: Which of the following methods gives the highest purity and yield of chlorobenzene from aniline?
Gattermann Reaction.explanation: Sandmeyer reaction provides significantly higher yields ($75-80\%$) and fewer biaryl/tarry byproducts than the Gattermann reaction ($40-50\%$). Direct chlorination of aniline causes oxidation and polychlorination.

Gattermann Reaction.question: What visual observation indicates that the Gattermann reaction is taking place when copper powder is added to the diazonium solution?

options.text: Brisk effervescence of a colorless gas ($\text{N}_2$) and disappearance of the red/orange diazonium color
Immediate precipitation of bright yellow sulfur
The solution turns into a solid black mass
Rapid evolution of purple iodine vapors

Gattermann Reaction.explanation: As copper powder initiates electron transfer, rapid evolution of nitrogen gas causes vigorous bubbling and effervescence while the diazonium salt is converted to haloarene.

Gattermann Reaction.question: Treatment of m-nitrobenzenediazonium chloride with $\text{Cu}$ powder and concentrated $\text{HBr}$ gives:
Gattermann Reaction.explanation: The reaction occurs with 100% regioselectivity at the position of the diazonium group, yielding 1-bromo-3-nitrobenzene.

Gattermann Reaction.question: Why is copper powder washed with ether or acetone and dried before being added in the Gattermann reaction?

options.text: To oxidize copper to cupric oxide
To convert copper into copper acetylide
To remove surface organic impurities and ensure free-flowing, unagglomerated metallic particles

Gattermann Reaction.explanation: Clean, dry copper powder disperses evenly throughout the aqueous acidic reaction mixture, maximizing the surface contact area with the diazonium ions.

Gattermann Reaction.question: In the Gattermann reaction of benzenediazonium hydrogen sulfate ($	ext{ArN}_2^+	ext{HSO}_4^-$) with $\text{HCl}$ and $\text{Cu}$, what haloarene is formed?
Gattermann Reaction.explanation: The halide ion present in excess in the solution ($Cl^-$ from $HCl$) is transferred to the aryl radical on the copper surface, producing chlorobenzene.

Gattermann Reaction.question: Which of the following diazonium salts is the most stable and can be isolated as a dry solid at room temperature?
Gattermann Reaction.explanation: Benzenediazonium tetrafluoroborate is an insoluble, stable crystalline salt at room temperature that does not explode upon handling, making it uniquely safe among diazonium salts.

Gattermann Reaction.question: Can aliphatic primary amines be converted into chloroalkanes via the Gattermann reaction?

options.text: No, aliphatic diazonium salts are extremely unstable and decompose instantaneously even at $0^\circ\text{C}$ to give carbocations, alcohols, and alkenes
Yes, but only if they contain an odd number of carbons

Gattermann Reaction.explanation: Aliphatic diazonium salts lack resonance stabilization; loss of $N_2$ occurs immediately upon formation, yielding complex mixtures of alcohols, alkenes, and alkyl halides via carbocations.

Gattermann Reaction.question: What is the oxidation state of copper in the initial copper powder used in the Gattermann reaction?
Gattermann Reaction.explanation: Copper powder is metallic copper in the elemental oxidation state $Cu(0)$.

Gattermann Reaction.question: During the Gattermann reaction, some copper powder dissolves to form a green/blue solution due to the formation of:
Gattermann Reaction.explanation: Single-electron transfer and oxidation by air/acid converts some copper into hydrated copper(II) ions ($Cu^{2+}$), imparting a characteristic blue-green color to the aqueous solution.

Gattermann Reaction.question: Which of the following compounds is the starting material for preparing benzenediazonium chloride?
Gattermann Reaction.explanation: Aniline undergoes diazotization when treated with sodium nitrite and hydrochloric acid at $0-5^\circ C$ to form benzenediazonium chloride.

Gattermann Reaction.question: What reagent generates the nitrosonium ion ($\text{NO}^+$) required for diazotizing aniline prior to the Gattermann reaction?
Gattermann Reaction.explanation: Nitrous acid ($HNO_2$), generated in situ from $NaNO_2$ and $HCl$, is protonated and loses water to form the electrophilic nitrosonium ion ($NO^+$), which attacks the amino group of aniline.

Gattermann Reaction.question: What is the temperature range strictly maintained during the diazotization step of the Gattermann process?
Gattermann Reaction.explanation: To prevent rapid thermal decomposition of benzenediazonium chloride into phenol and nitrogen gas, the temperature is maintained strictly between $0^\circ C$ and $5^\circ C$ using an ice bath.

Gattermann Reaction.question: What is the product when 2,4,6-tribromoaniline is diazotized and treated with copper powder and hypophosphorous acid ($\text{H}_3\text{PO}_2$)?
Gattermann Reaction.explanation: Hypophosphorous acid ($H_3PO_2$) acts as a reducing agent that replaces the diazonium group with hydrogen (reductive deamination), cleanly producing 1,3,5-tribromobenzene.

Gattermann Reaction.question: Which of the following represents the correct order of steps to synthesize bromobenzene from benzene via the Gattermann route?
Gattermann Reaction.explanation: The synthetic pathway is: Nitration of benzene $\rightarrow$ Reduction of nitrobenzene to aniline $\rightarrow$ Diazotization of aniline to benzenediazonium chloride $\rightarrow$ Gattermann reaction with $Cu/HBr$ to yield bromobenzene.

Gattermann Reaction.question: In the Gattermann reaction, what role does concentrated $\text{HCl}$ or $\text{HBr}$ play beyond providing the halide ion?

options.text: It maintains a low pH to keep diazonium ions stable and provides an acidic medium for the surface redox cycle of copper
It prevents the evolution of nitrogen gas

Gattermann Reaction.explanation: Strong mineral acid prevents diazoamino side reactions, ensures complete protonation of any unreacted amine, and provides the halide counterions needed to trap the aryl radical on the copper surface.

Gattermann Reaction.question: What is the major side product when benzenediazonium chloride is treated with copper powder in the absence of sufficient halogen acid?
Gattermann Reaction.explanation: In the absence of sufficient halide ions, aryl radicals react with water to form phenol or dimerize with each other to yield biphenyl.

Gattermann Reaction.question: Why is Gattermann reaction considered a regioselective substitution?

options.text: It always yields the meta isomer exclusively
It introduces halogen at all positions simultaneously
The halogen migrates around the ring until it finds the most stable carbon
The incoming halogen atom occupies precisely the position formerly occupied by the amino/diazonium group without any positional isomerization

Gattermann Reaction.explanation: Because the aryl radical is generated directly at the carbon that lost the nitrogen molecule, the halogen is trapped specifically at that same carbon with 100% regiocontrol.

Gattermann Reaction.question: Which of the following statements about the Gattermann reaction is FALSE?

options.text: It is a nucleophilic addition to a carbonyl group
It is catalyzed by metallic copper powder
It involves the evolution of nitrogen gas
It proceeds via an aryl free radical intermediate

Gattermann Reaction.explanation: The Gattermann reaction is an aromatic radical substitution/displacement of a diazonium group, completely unrelated to carbonyl chemistry.

Gattermann Reaction.question: Can p-hydroxybenzenediazonium salts undergo Gattermann reaction cleanly without coupling?

options.text: No, because the strongly activated phenolic ring rapidly undergoes azo-coupling with diazonium ions to form colored azo dyes
No, because phenols are insoluble in water

Gattermann Reaction.explanation: Phenols are extremely electron-rich and readily undergo electrophilic coupling with diazonium salts (azo coupling) rather than simple displacement by halogen.

Gattermann Reaction.question: What is the appearance of chlorobenzene produced via the Gattermann reaction?

options.text: A colorless, volatile liquid with an almond-like odor ($bp\ 132^\circ\text{C}$)

Gattermann Reaction.explanation: Chlorobenzene is a clear, colorless liquid with a characteristic sweet aromatic odor that boils at $132^\circ C$.

Gattermann Reaction.question: Which of the following reactions uses the same starting material (arenediazonium salt) as the Gattermann reaction?
Gattermann Reaction.explanation: Sandmeyer, Balz-Schiemann, and Gomberg-Bachmann reactions all start with arenediazonium salts to introduce halogens or biaryl linkages.

Gattermann Reaction.question: What is the primary synthetic significance of the Gattermann and Sandmeyer reactions in aromatic organic synthesis?

options.text: They allow the replacement of a primary aromatic amino group ($-\text{NH}_2$) by halogen ($-Cl, -Br$), providing a route to haloarenes that cannot be prepared by direct electrophilic halogenation
They selectively reduce carboxylic acids to aldehydes
They break aromatic rings into aliphatic chains

Gattermann Reaction.explanation: Because $-NO_2$ can be directed meta and $-NH_2$ can be directed ortho/para, converting them via diazotization and Gattermann/Sandmeyer enables the synthesis of substituted haloarenes (e.g., m-bromonitrobenzene or o-chlorotoluene) impossible by direct halogenation.

Fittig Reaction.question: What are the primary reactants and conditions for the classical Fittig reaction?

options.text: Two molecules of an aryl halide treated with sodium metal in dry ether at reflux
An aryl halide and an alkyl halide with sodium in dry ether
Two molecules of an alkyl halide with sodium in dry ether
An aryl halide treated with magnesium in wet ether

Fittig Reaction.explanation: The Fittig reaction involves the homocoupling of two aryl halide molecules using metallic sodium in dry ether: $2Ar-X + 2Na \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} Ar-Ar + 2NaX$.

Fittig Reaction.question: What is the major organic product formed when chlorobenzene is heated with sodium in dry ether?
Fittig Reaction.explanation: Two phenyl rings couple together with elimination of sodium chloride: $2C_6H_5Cl + 2Na \rightarrow C_6H_5-C_6H_5 + 2NaCl$.

Fittig Reaction.question: What is the product when 1-bromonaphthalene is subjected to the Fittig reaction?
Fittig Reaction.explanation: Homocoupling of two 1-naphthyl radicals/species across the C-1 position yields 1,1'-binaphthyl.

Fittig Reaction.question: What product is obtained when 2-chlorotoluene (o-chlorotoluene) undergoes the Fittig reaction?
Fittig Reaction.explanation: Coupling occurs at the chlorine-bearing carbon (position 1), joining two o-tolyl rings to give 2,2'-dimethylbiphenyl.

Fittig Reaction.question: What product is obtained when 4-bromotoluene (p-bromotoluene) undergoes the Fittig reaction?
Fittig Reaction.explanation: Coupling occurs at the 4-position of both rings, cleanly yielding 4,4'-dimethylbiphenyl.

Fittig Reaction.question: How does the Fittig reaction differ from the Ullmann reaction?

options.text: Fittig reaction produces alkanes, whereas Ullmann produces biaryls
Fittig uses sodium metal in dry ether, whereas Ullmann uses copper powder at high temperatures ($>200^\circ\text{C}$)
Fittig uses zinc dust in water, whereas Ullmann uses sodium
There is no difference; they are exact synonyms

Fittig Reaction.explanation: The Fittig reaction utilizes metallic sodium in dry ether, whereas the Ullmann biaryl synthesis employs activated copper powder in a sealed tube or high-boiling solvent (typically with iodobenzene).

Fittig Reaction.question: What is the relative reactivity order of haloarenes in the Fittig reaction?

options.text: All haloarenes react at identical rates

Fittig Reaction.explanation: Iodoarenes have the weakest carbon-halogen bond ($C-I$) and undergo single electron reduction by sodium most readily, whereas fluoroarenes are essentially inert.

Fittig Reaction.question: Why can Fittig reaction NOT be carried out in protic solvents like ethanol or water?

options.text: Biaryls are soluble only in water
Ethanol causes halogenation of the aromatic ring
Aryl halides undergo rapid $S_N2$ substitution with ethanol
Sodium metal decomposes vigorously, and the arylsodium intermediate is instantly protonated to form benzene

Fittig Reaction.explanation: Active sodium reacts violently with protic solvents. Furthermore, the strongly basic organosodium species ($	ext{Ar}^-	ext{Na}^+$) is immediately protonated to the parent arene ($	ext{Ar}-H$).

Fittig Reaction.question: What is the reactive intermediate in the mechanism of the Fittig reaction?

options.text: Aryl free radical ($\text{Ar}^\bullet$) and arylsodium ($\text{Ar-Na}$) intermediate

Fittig Reaction.explanation: Single-electron transfer from sodium to the haloarene produces an aryl free radical and sodium halide; further reduction generates arylsodium, which couples with another haloarene or aryl radical.

Fittig Reaction.question: What is the molecular formula of biphenyl, the product of the Fittig reaction of chlorobenzene?
Fittig Reaction.explanation: Each phenyl ring has formula $C_6H_5$. Coupling two phenyl rings gives $C_6H_5-C_6H_5 = C_{12}H_{10}$.

Fittig Reaction.question: In biphenyl in the gas phase or in solution, the two phenyl rings are not strictly coplanar because of:

options.text: Steric repulsion between the ortho-hydrogen atoms of the two adjacent phenyl rings
A triple bond between the two rings

Fittig Reaction.explanation: In the planar conformation, the four ortho hydrogens (positions 2, 2', 6, 6') collide sterically. To minimize this steric hindrance, the two rings twist by approximately $40-45^\circ$ relative to each other.

Fittig Reaction.question: What phenomenon occurs when bulky substituents (e.g., $-\text{NO}_2, -\text{COOH}$) are present at all four ortho positions (2, 2', 6, 6') of a biphenyl prepared via Fittig coupling?

options.text: Atropisomerism (restricted rotation resulting in isolable enantiomers / axial chirality)

Fittig Reaction.explanation: Bulky ortho substituents create a massive steric barrier that prevents rotation about the central $C-C$ single bond, giving rise to optically active, separable enantiomers (atropisomers).

Fittig Reaction.question: What is the product when 1-chloro-4-nitrobenzene is subjected to Fittig reaction conditions?
Fittig Reaction.explanation: Coupling occurs at the 1-position where the chlorine atom was located, producing 4,4'-dinitrobiphenyl.

Fittig Reaction.question: Can fluorobenzene be coupled to biphenyl using sodium in dry ether under normal Fittig conditions?

options.text: Yes, it gives a quantitative yield at $0^\circ\text{C}$
No, the $\text{C-F}$ bond is too strong to undergo reduction by sodium
Yes, it is the most reactive haloarene

Fittig Reaction.explanation: The $C-F$ bond has high bond dissociation energy and significant partial double bond character due to $2p-2p$ resonance, making it inert under standard Fittig conditions.

Fittig Reaction.question: Which of the following haloarenes gives 3,3'-dimethylbiphenyl upon Fittig coupling?
Fittig Reaction.explanation: Homocoupling of 3-bromotoluene joins the two 3-methylphenyl rings at C-1, yielding 3,3'-dimethylbiphenyl.

Fittig Reaction.question: What is the physical appearance of pure biphenyl obtained from the Fittig reaction?

options.text: Colorless/white crystalline solid with a sweet, pleasant characteristic aroma

Fittig Reaction.explanation: Biphenyl forms white pearlescent crystalline flakes with a melting point of $69-70^\circ C$ and a pleasant floral odor.

Fittig Reaction.question: In the Fittig reaction of bromobenzene, what inorganic salt precipitates out of the ether solution?
Fittig Reaction.explanation: The bromine atoms combine with sodium: $2C_6H_5Br + 2Na \rightarrow C_6H_5-C_6H_5 + 2NaBr\downarrow$.

Fittig Reaction.question: What is the role of refluxing the dry ether in the Fittig reaction?

options.text: To evaporate the ether and leave pure biphenyl
To provide sufficient activation energy to break the strong aromatic carbon-halogen bond
To oxidize sodium to sodium peroxide
To prevent the precipitation of sodium bromide

Fittig Reaction.explanation: Aryl $C-X$ bonds are much stronger than alkyl $C-X$ bonds; heating at the reflux temperature of ether (or higher-boiling ethers like THF or dioxane) is necessary to achieve adequate reaction rates.

Fittig Reaction.question: Treatment of 2-bromobiphenyl with sodium in dry ether yields:
Fittig Reaction.explanation: Coupling of two 2-biphenylyl moieties joins the two units into a 4-ring chain: o-quaterphenyl.

Fittig Reaction.question: Which of the following compounds is produced when 2,2'-dibromobiphenyl is treated with sodium in dry ether?
Fittig Reaction.explanation: Intramolecular coupling between the 2 and 2' positions closes a central 4-membered ring between the two benzene rings, forming biphenylene.

Fittig Reaction.question: Why does the Fittig reaction generally require more vigorous conditions than the aliphatic Wurtz reaction?

options.text: The carbon-halogen bond in haloarenes has partial double-bond character due to resonance donation of the halogen lone pairs into the aromatic $\pi$-cloud
Aryl halides are completely insoluble in ether
Sodium cannot donate electrons to aromatic rings
Biphenyl is explosive at room temperature

Fittig Reaction.explanation: Resonance delocalization gives the $C_{sp^2}-X$ bond significant double-bond character ($15-20\%$), making it shorter and much stronger than an aliphatic $C_{sp^3}-X$ single bond.

Fittig Reaction.question: When an equimolar mixture of chlorobenzene and 4-chlorotoluene is treated with sodium in dry ether, how many biaryl products are formed?
Fittig Reaction.explanation: Cross-Fittig coupling yields self-coupling products (biphenyl and 4,4'-dimethylbiphenyl) as well as the cross-coupling product (4-methylbiphenyl).

Fittig Reaction.question: What is the formal oxidation state of the carbon atom bonded to chlorine in chlorobenzene versus the corresponding carbon in biphenyl?

options.text: There is no change in oxidation state
It is reduced from $0$ to $-1$ (or gains electron density from sodium)

Fittig Reaction.explanation: In chlorobenzene, carbon is bonded to a more electronegative chlorine atom (assigned $+1$ contribution). In biphenyl, it is bonded to another carbon (zero contribution). Thus, the ring carbon is formally reduced by the sodium metal.

Fittig Reaction.question: Can iodobenzene undergo Fittig-type coupling at room temperature?

options.text: No, iodobenzene never reacts with metals
No, it only reacts under gamma irradiation
No, iodobenzene is an explosive solid
Yes, iodobenzene is much more reactive and can react with sodium or lithium without prolonged vigorous boiling

Fittig Reaction.explanation: Because the $C-I$ bond is relatively weak, iodobenzene undergoes single-electron reduction readily, even at room temperature.

Fittig Reaction.question: Which of the following metals can promote Fittig coupling of haloarenes similarly to sodium?
Fittig Reaction.explanation: Lithium in ether cleanly converts aryl halides to aryllithium, which can couple to form biaryls.

Fittig Reaction.question: What is the primary industrial application of biphenyl and its mixture with diphenyl ether (Dowtherm A)?
Fittig Reaction.explanation: The eutectic mixture of biphenyl ($26.5\%$) and diphenyl ether ($73.5\%$), known as Dowtherm A or Therminol VP-1, is a widely used liquid/vapor heat transfer medium up to $400^\circ C$.

Fittig Reaction.question: When 2-chloro-1,3-dimethylbenzene (2-chlorom-xylene) undergoes Fittig reaction, what makes the coupling sluggish?

options.text: Steric hindrance from the two ortho methyl groups flanking the reaction center

Fittig Reaction.explanation: Both ortho positions are occupied by methyl groups, which sterically shield the reaction center and severely hinder the approach of another aryl fragment.

Fittig Reaction.question: Which of the following solvents is best suited for Fittig reactions requiring higher temperatures than diethyl ether?
Fittig Reaction.explanation: Dry THF ($bp\ 66^\circ C$) and dry 1,4-dioxane ($bp\ 101^\circ C$) are cyclic aprotic ethers that dissolve organometallics well and allow higher reflux temperatures than diethyl ether ($bp\ 35^\circ C$).

Fittig Reaction.question: Treatment of 9-bromoanthracene with sodium in dry ether produces:
Fittig Reaction.explanation: Coupling at the active meso position (C-9) joins two anthracene units to form 9,9'-bianthryl.

Fittig Reaction.question: What side reaction can occur if traces of oxygen/air are present during a Fittig reaction?

options.text: Formation of phenols and phenolic polymers via reaction of aryl radicals/arylsodium with $\text{O}_2$
Complete conversion of ether to water

Fittig Reaction.explanation: Aryl radicals and arylsodium react rapidly with molecular oxygen to form peroxy species ($Ar-O-O^-$) that break down to phenols, diminishing the biaryl yield.

Fittig Reaction.question: Which of the following compounds CANNOT undergo Fittig reaction?
Fittig Reaction.explanation: The acidic protons on the $-\text{NH}_2$ group ($pK_a \approx 27-30$) react with sodium metal or protonate arylsodium, interfering with the coupling reaction.

Fittig Reaction.question: Reaction of 2-bromothiophene with sodium in dry ether yields:
Fittig Reaction.explanation: Heteroaryl halides also undergo the Fittig reaction; 2-bromothiophene couples to yield 2,2'-bithiophene.

Fittig Reaction.question: In the Fittig reaction of 1-bromonaphthalene, what is the spatial orientation of the two naphthalene rings in 1,1'-binaphthyl?

options.text: They are held almost perpendicular to each other due to severe steric clash between the 8 and 8' peri-hydrogens
They are completely coplanar in a single flat plane
They form an angle of exactly $180^\circ$
The rings fuse together into perylene spontaneously

Fittig Reaction.explanation: The peri-hydrogens at positions 8 and 8' and ortho-hydrogens at 2 and 2' collide strongly, forcing the two naphthalene planes to adopt a near-perpendicular twisted geometry (axial chirality).

Fittig Reaction.question: Optically pure $(R)$- and $(S)$-enantiomers of 1,1'-binaphthyl derivatives (such as BINAP and BINOL) owe their optical activity to:

options.text: Restricted rotation around the biaryl axis (Atropisomerism)
Helical twisting of a single ring

Fittig Reaction.explanation: The bulky binaphthyl framework cannot rotate past the peri/ortho hydrogens at room temperature, creating stable, non-superimposable mirror-image enantiomers.

Fittig Reaction.question: What happens when chlorobenzene is treated with sodium amalgam ($\text{Na-Hg}$) and water?
Fittig Reaction.explanation: In the presence of a protic source (water), sodium amalgam acts as a reducing agent that replaces halogen with hydrogen, reducing chlorobenzene to benzene without biaryl coupling.

Fittig Reaction.question: Which of the following compounds gives biphenyl when treated with sodium in dry ether?
Fittig Reaction.explanation: Bromobenzene is the quintessential aryl halide that dimerizes to biphenyl via the Fittig reaction.

Fittig Reaction.question: What is the ratio of sodium atoms consumed to haloarene molecules in the balanced equation of the Fittig reaction?
Fittig Reaction.explanation: The stoichiometric equation is $2ArX + 2Na \rightarrow Ar-Ar + 2NaX$, which simplifies to a 1:1 molar ratio of sodium to haloarene.

Fittig Reaction.question: Coupling of 4-chloroanisole with sodium in dry ether affords:
Fittig Reaction.explanation: Coupling of two 4-methoxyphenyl radicals/anions yields 4,4'-dimethoxybiphenyl.

Fittig Reaction.question: Why is potassium metal rarely used instead of sodium in the Fittig reaction in standard laboratories?

options.text: Potassium does not react with aryl halides
Potassium is much more dangerously reactive, highly pyrophoric, and prone to forming explosive peroxides/superoxides
Potassium halides are insoluble in all solvents

Fittig Reaction.explanation: Metallic potassium is significantly more hazardous, reacts violently with dry ether on prolonged contact, and can form shock-sensitive potassium superoxide on its surface.

Fittig Reaction.question: Which modern transition-metal-catalyzed cross-coupling has largely superseded the Fittig reaction for synthesizing unsymmetrical and functionalized biaryls?
Fittig Reaction.explanation: The palladium-catalyzed Suzuki-Miyaura coupling between arylboronic acids and aryl halides operates under mild conditions with exceptional functional group tolerance, avoiding the harshness of metallic sodium.

Fittig Reaction.question: When 2,4-dinitrochlorobenzene is treated with sodium in dry ether, Fittig coupling fails primarily because:

options.text: The strongly electron-withdrawing nitro groups stabilize Meisenheimer-type radical anions, leading to complex decomposition and side reactions
Chlorine cannot be cleaved by sodium
The compound sublimates at room temperature

Fittig Reaction.explanation: Polynitro haloarenes undergo electron transfer to form deeply colored, explosive radical anion salts rather than cleanly coupling to biaryls.

Fittig Reaction.question: What is the major product when 1-chloro-2-phenylethene ($\beta$-chlorostyrene) undergoes sodium coupling?
Fittig Reaction.explanation: Vinyl halides couple similarly to aryl halides with sodium in ether, dimerizing $\beta$-chlorostyrene to the conjugated diene 1,4-diphenylbuta-1,3-diene.

Fittig Reaction.question: In the Fittig reaction of bromobenzene, what test can be performed to verify the formation of biphenyl?

options.text: Testing for unsaturation with bromine water (decolorization)
Determination of the sharp melting point at $69-70^\circ\text{C}$ and absence of halogen in sodium fusion extract

Fittig Reaction.explanation: Pure biphenyl is a neutral aromatic solid with a sharp melting point of $69-70^\circ C$ that gives a negative Lassaigne's test for halogen.

Fittig Reaction.question: How is unreacted haloarene separated from the product biphenyl in a laboratory Fittig reaction?

options.text: By treating with dilute hydrochloric acid
By freezing the solution in liquid nitrogen
By fractional distillation under reduced pressure or recrystallization from ethanol

Fittig Reaction.explanation: Haloarenes like chlorobenzene ($bp\ 132^\circ C$) or bromobenzene ($bp\ 156^\circ C$) are volatile liquids, whereas biphenyl is a crystalline solid ($bp\ 255^\circ C$); fractional distillation or recrystallization from ethanol cleanly isolates pure biphenyl.

Fittig Reaction.question: What is the role of ultrasonication in modern modifications of the Fittig reaction?

options.text: It cleans the surface of metallic sodium, dispersing it into fine particles to increase surface area and accelerate coupling
It generates UV light to cleave $C-C$ bonds
It prevents the formation of sodium halides

Fittig Reaction.explanation: Ultrasonic cavitation mechanically scours the passivating layer of sodium halide off the metal surface, dramatically improving mass transfer and reaction rate.

Wurtz Reaction.question: What are the primary reagents used in the classical Wurtz reaction?

options.text: Zinc dust in dilute hydrochloric acid

Wurtz Reaction.explanation: The Wurtz reaction involves treating alkyl halides with metallic sodium in dry ether: $2RX + 2Na \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} R-R + 2NaX$.

Wurtz Reaction.question: Which of the following alkanes CANNOT be prepared by the Wurtz reaction?
Wurtz Reaction.explanation: The Wurtz reaction joins two carbon radicals or carbanions; hence the smallest possible product alkane contains two carbon atoms (ethane). Methane, having only one carbon, cannot be synthesized.

Wurtz Reaction.question: Why is 'dry ether' strictly required as the solvent in the Wurtz reaction?

options.text: Ether catalyzes the reaction by donating hydride ions
Water prevents the dissolution of alkyl halides
Sodium metal and the organosodium intermediate react vigorously with water, destroying the reagents and giving alkanes by protonation
Ether acts as an oxidizing agent

Wurtz Reaction.explanation: Sodium reacts violently with water to form $NaOH$ and $H_2$. Furthermore, moisture protonates the organosodium intermediate ($R-Na + H_2O \rightarrow R-H + NaOH$), preventing $C-C$ coupling.

Wurtz Reaction.question: Which type of alkane is obtained in the best yield via the Wurtz reaction?

options.text: Unsymmetrical alkanes with an odd number of carbon atoms
Symmetrical alkanes containing an even number of carbon atoms

Wurtz Reaction.explanation: Coupling of two identical alkyl halide molecules ($R-X + R-X$) cleanly yields a symmetrical alkane ($R-R$) containing an even number of carbon atoms without forming hard-to-separate mixtures.

Wurtz Reaction.question: When a mixture of bromoethane and 1-bromopropane is treated with sodium in dry ether, how many different alkanes are formed?

options.text: Four: Ethane, Propane, Butane, and Pentane

Wurtz Reaction.explanation: Self-coupling of bromoethane gives butane ($C_4$); self-coupling of 1-bromopropane gives hexane ($C_6$); and cross-coupling between the two gives pentane ($C_5$).

Wurtz Reaction.question: Why is the Wurtz reaction NOT suitable for the preparation of unsymmetrical alkanes like propane or pentane?

options.text: Unsymmetrical alkanes are thermodynamically unstable and explode
A mixture of three alkanes is formed whose boiling points are very close, making fractional distillation extremely difficult
The cross-coupling product is never formed
Sodium only reacts with even-numbered alkyl halides

Wurtz Reaction.explanation: Cross-Wurtz reaction gives a mixture of self-coupling and cross-coupling products ($R_1-R_1, R_1-R_2, R_2-R_2$) in comparable yields, which are difficult to separate into pure components.

Wurtz Reaction.question: What is the major organic product when 2-bromopropane is treated with sodium in dry ether?
Wurtz Reaction.explanation: Coupling of two isopropyl radicals $(CH_3)_2CH^\bullet$ yields 2,3-dimethylbutane as the major coupling product.

Wurtz Reaction.question: When tert-butyl bromide is treated with sodium in dry ether, the major product is NOT 2,2,3,3-tetramethylbutane, but rather:
Wurtz Reaction.explanation: The organosodium intermediate acts as an extremely strong base, and steric hindrance prevents $S_N2$ displacement at the tertiary carbon; hence $E2$ elimination dominates, yielding isobutylene.

Wurtz Reaction.question: What are the two accepted mechanistic pathways for the Wurtz reaction?

options.text: Free radical pathway and organometallic (ionic / carbanion) pathway
Oxidative addition followed by reductive elimination via palladium

Wurtz Reaction.explanation: The reaction involves single-electron transfer (SET) to generate free radicals ($R^\bullet$) which can dimerize, or form an alkylsodium intermediate ($R-Na$) that displaces halide from another $RX$ via $S_N2$.

Wurtz Reaction.question: Treatment of 1,3-dibromopropane with sodium in dry ether affords:
Wurtz Reaction.explanation: Intramolecular Wurtz coupling between C-1 and C-3 of the propane chain closes a 3-membered ring, producing cyclopropane.

Wurtz Reaction.question: Treatment of 1,4-dibromobutane with sodium in dry ether affords:
Wurtz Reaction.explanation: Intramolecular Wurtz coupling between the terminal carbons of 1,4-dibromobutane cyclizes to yield cyclobutane.

Wurtz Reaction.question: What side products are formed in the Wurtz reaction due to disproportionation of secondary alkyl radicals?

options.text: An alkane and an alkene containing the same number of carbon atoms (e.g., propane and propene)

Wurtz Reaction.explanation: Two alkyl radicals can undergo hydrogen atom abstraction (disproportionation): $R-CH_2-CH_2^\bullet + R-CH_2-CH_2^\bullet \rightarrow R-CH_2-CH_3 + R-CH=CH_2$.

Wurtz Reaction.question: Which halogen in alkyl halides undergoes the Wurtz reaction most readily?

options.text: All alkyl halides react at identical rates
Alkyl iodides do not react with sodium

Wurtz Reaction.explanation: Because the $C-I$ bond is the weakest and iodide is the best leaving group, alkyl iodides have the highest reactivity in the Wurtz reaction.

Wurtz Reaction.question: What is the product when 1-bromo-3-chlorocyclobutane is treated with sodium in dry ether?
Wurtz Reaction.explanation: Intramolecular coupling across the diagonal C-1 and C-3 positions of the cyclobutane ring produces the highly strained bicyclic hydrocarbon bicyclo[1.1.0]butane.

Wurtz Reaction.question: Treatment of 1-bromobutane with sodium in dry ether gives:
Wurtz Reaction.explanation: Coupling of two 1-butyl groups ($CH_3(CH_2)_3-$) yields the straight-chain symmetrical alkane n-octane.

Wurtz Reaction.question: The Wurtz reaction of methyl iodide gives:
Wurtz Reaction.explanation: Two methyl groups couple together: $2CH_3I + 2Na \rightarrow CH_3-CH_3 + 2NaI$.

Wurtz Reaction.question: Which of the following compounds gives a single alkane upon reaction with sodium in dry ether?

options.text: A mixture of chloromethane and chloroethane

Wurtz Reaction.explanation: A pure single alkyl halide (1-chloropropane) couples with itself to yield solely hexane as the coupling product.

Wurtz Reaction.question: Frankland reaction is an analogue of the Wurtz reaction that uses which metal instead of sodium?
Wurtz Reaction.explanation: The Frankland reaction employs zinc metal: $2RX + Zn \rightarrow R-R + ZnX_2$, proceeding via dialkylzinc intermediates ($R_2Zn$).

Wurtz Reaction.question: What is the product when 1,6-dibromohexane is heated with sodium in dry ether?
Wurtz Reaction.explanation: Intramolecular coupling between the terminal carbons of the 6-carbon chain smoothly forms the strain-free 6-membered ring of cyclohexane.

Wurtz Reaction.question: Why does the yield of alkane decrease significantly from primary to secondary to tertiary alkyl halides in the Wurtz reaction?

options.text: Tertiary halides do not react with sodium metal
Tertiary halides form stable free radicals that do not react
Steric hindrance increases the tendency toward E2 elimination and disproportionation rather than substitution/coupling

Wurtz Reaction.explanation: With increasing steric bulk, the nucleophilic attack ($S_N2$) of the organosodium intermediate becomes hindered, favoring base-induced $E2$ elimination to alkenes.

Wurtz Reaction.question: In the preparation of ethane by Wurtz reaction, what gas can be detected as a minor byproduct due to radical disproportionation if traces of higher radicals are present?
Wurtz Reaction.explanation: While methyl radicals cannot disproportionate, with ethyl or higher halides, disproportionation yields an alkene (ethene) alongside the alkane.

Wurtz Reaction.question: Can aryl halides undergo the standard Wurtz reaction to form alkanes?

options.text: No, coupling of aryl halides with sodium is termed the Fittig reaction and produces diaryls (e.g., biphenyl)
No, aryl halides do not react with sodium at all

Wurtz Reaction.explanation: Aryl halides alone coupled by sodium give biaryls (Fittig reaction); alkyl halides alone give alkanes (Wurtz reaction).

Wurtz Reaction.question: Which of the following metals can replace sodium in dry ether to perform coupling of alkyl halides?
Wurtz Reaction.explanation: Active alkali metals like lithium or potassium can similarly reduce alkyl halides to form organometallic intermediates and coupled alkanes.

Wurtz Reaction.question: Corey-House synthesis is superior to the Wurtz reaction because:

options.text: It does not require any organic halides
It uses water as the primary solvent
It generates methane from carbon dioxide
It cleanly synthesizes both symmetrical and unsymmetrical alkanes in high yield without forming complex mixtures

Wurtz Reaction.explanation: Corey-House synthesis uses lithium dialkylcuprates ($R_2CuLi$, Gilman reagents) to couple cleanly with primary alkyl halides ($R'X$) to yield specific unsymmetrical alkanes $R-R'$ without cross-mixture problems.

Wurtz Reaction.question: What is the major product when neopentyl bromide is treated with sodium in dry ether?
Wurtz Reaction.explanation: Coupling of two neopentyl radicals $(CH_3)_3C-CH_2^\bullet$ gives the symmetrical, highly branched alkane 2,2,5,5-tetramethylhexane.

Wurtz Reaction.question: What observation confirms that free radical intermediates are formed during the Wurtz reaction?

options.text: Trapping of radicals by radical scavengers and observation of rearranged/disproportionated side products
The reaction mixture turns brightly fluorescent
Immediate formation of a white precipitate of sodium hydride

Wurtz Reaction.explanation: Radical scavengers inhibit coupling, and the formation of alkene + alkane disproportionation products is classic evidence for radical intermediates.

Wurtz Reaction.question: Which of the following alkyl halides yields 2,3-dimethylbutane upon Wurtz reaction?
Wurtz Reaction.explanation: Coupling of two 2-propyl moieties ($(CH_3)_2CH-$) forms $(CH_3)_2CH-CH(CH_3)_2$, which is 2,3-dimethylbutane.

Wurtz Reaction.question: Which of the following alkyl halides yields 3,4-dimethylhexane upon Wurtz reaction?
Wurtz Reaction.explanation: Coupling of two sec-butyl groups ($CH_3-CH_2-CH(CH_3)-$): $2\text{C}_4\text{H}_9\text{Br} + 2\text{Na} \rightarrow CH_3CH_2CH(CH_3)-CH(CH_3)CH_2CH_3$, which is 3,4-dimethylhexane.

Wurtz Reaction.question: Wurtz reaction of an equimolar mixture of $\text{CH}_3\text{I}$ and $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{I}$ yields:
Wurtz Reaction.explanation: Self-coupling produces ethane ($CH_3-CH_3$) and butane ($C_2H_5-C_2H_5$), while cross-coupling produces propane ($CH_3-C_2H_5$).

Wurtz Reaction.question: Why does fluoromethane fail to give good yields of ethane in the Wurtz reaction?

options.text: The $\text{C-F}$ bond is extremely strong ($485\text{ kJ/mol}$) and resists single-electron transfer cleavage by sodium
Sodium fluoride dissolves in dry ether
Fluorine oxidizes sodium to sodium superoxide

Wurtz Reaction.explanation: The exceptionally high bond dissociation energy of the carbon-fluorine bond makes it inert to reduction by sodium under standard Wurtz conditions.

Wurtz Reaction.question: In the Wurtz reaction of optically active $(S)\text{-2-bromobutane}$, the 3,4-dimethylhexane product obtained is:

options.text: A single optically pure $(S,S)$-enantiomer with 100% retention
A mixture of diastereomers: the meso compound and the $(d,l)$-enantiomeric pair

Wurtz Reaction.explanation: Because the intermediate sec-butyl radical or carbanion is planar/rapidly inverting, coupling of $(R)$ and $(S)$ fragments produces $(R,R)$, $(S,S)$ enantiomers and the achiral $(R,S)$-meso diastereomer.

Wurtz Reaction.question: What is the function of dry ether in the Wurtz reaction beyond dissolving the organic reactants?

options.text: It donates protons to terminate the reaction
It acts as a phase-transfer catalyst for sodium halides
It evaporates to drive the reaction to the right by entropy
It coordinates with and stabilizes the electropositive sodium cation ($\text{Na}^+$) without reacting with the carbanion

Wurtz Reaction.explanation: Ether is an aprotic Lewis base whose oxygen lone pairs solvate the $Na^+$ cations, allowing the reactive carbanions/organosodium species to exist long enough to couple.

Wurtz Reaction.question: Which of the following compounds CANNOT be synthesized in high yield by the Wurtz reaction?
Wurtz Reaction.explanation: Neopentane has an odd number of carbons (5 carbons) and is unsymmetrical; attempting to prepare it via methyl halide + tert-butyl halide yields mainly isobutylene, ethane, and 2,2,3,3-tetramethylbutane.

Wurtz Reaction.question: When 1,2-dibromoethane is treated with sodium in dry ether, the major product formed is:
Wurtz Reaction.explanation: Instead of intermolecular coupling, 1,2-dihaloalkanes undergo rapid elimination of both halogen atoms to yield the corresponding alkene (ethene) and $2NaBr$.

Wurtz Reaction.question: When 1,5-dibromopentane is treated with sodium in dry ether, what is the major cyclic product?
Wurtz Reaction.explanation: Intramolecular coupling between the terminal carbons of the five-carbon chain produces cyclopentane.

Wurtz Reaction.question: Reaction of benzyl chloride with sodium in dry ether yields:
Wurtz Reaction.explanation: Coupling of two resonance-stabilized benzyl radicals ($C_6H_5-CH_2^\bullet$) yields 1,2-diphenylethane (bibenzyl).

Wurtz Reaction.question: The reaction of 2 moles of allyl bromide with sodium in dry ether gives:
Wurtz Reaction.explanation: Coupling of two allyl radicals ($CH_2=CH-CH_2^\bullet$) produces hexa-1,5-diene (diallyl).

Wurtz Reaction.question: Which of the following conditions would destroy the Wurtz reaction?

options.text: Presence of ethanol or water in the reaction mixture
Carrying out the reaction at room temperature

Wurtz Reaction.explanation: Protic solvents like ethanol or water protonate the alkyl carbanion immediately to form alkanes ($R-H$) and react violently with sodium metal.

Wurtz Reaction.question: What is the formal oxidation state change of the carbon bonded to halogen in $CH_3-Br$ when converted to $CH_3-CH_3$ via the Wurtz reaction?

options.text: There is no change in oxidation state

Wurtz Reaction.explanation: In bromomethane ($CH_3Br$), $C$ is bonded to $3H$ ($+1$ each) and $1Br$ ($-1$), giving oxidation state $-2$. In ethane ($CH_3-CH_3$), $C$ is bonded to $3H$ ($+1$ each) and $1C$ ($0$), giving oxidation state $-3$. The carbon is reduced by sodium.

Wurtz Reaction.question: Which alkyl halide gives n-hexane as the sole coupling product in the Wurtz reaction?
Wurtz Reaction.explanation: Self-coupling of two 3-carbon 1-bromopropane molecules gives $CH_3CH_2CH_2-CH_2CH_2CH_3$, which is n-hexane.

Wurtz Reaction.question: Treatment of 1-chloro-3-methylbutane with sodium in dry ether yields:
Wurtz Reaction.explanation: Coupling of two $(CH_3)_2CH-CH_2-CH_2-$ units joins the C-1 carbons, yielding $(CH_3)_2CH-(CH_2)_4-CH(CH_3)_2$, which is 2,7-dimethyloctane.

Wurtz Reaction.question: What type of reaction is the organometallic step ($R-Na + R-X \rightarrow R-R + NaX$) in the Wurtz reaction?
Wurtz Reaction.explanation: The carbanionic carbon of alkylsodium acts as a powerful nucleophile that displaces halide ion from the back side of an unhindered primary alkyl halide in an $S_N2$ step.

Wurtz Reaction.question: Which of the following alkanes can be prepared in high yield by the Wurtz reaction?

options.text: Propane from a mixture of methyl and ethyl iodides
Isobutane from methyl and isopropyl bromides

Wurtz Reaction.explanation: Bromoethane is a single primary alkyl halide that cleanly dimerizes to give symmetrical n-butane in high yield.

Wurtz Reaction.question: In the Wurtz reaction, sodium acts as a:
Wurtz Reaction.explanation: Metallic sodium ($Na$) readily loses its single valence electron ($Na \rightarrow Na^+ + e^-$) to reduce the alkyl halide, acting as a powerful reducing agent.

Wurtz Reaction.question: Why is the Wurtz reaction generally not used in the modern pharmaceutical industry to synthesize complex molecules?

options.text: Poor functional group tolerance due to the high reactivity of sodium, low yields with secondary/tertiary halides, and lack of stereocontrol
Alkanes cannot be used in pharmaceuticals
Sodium metal is too cheap to be patented
Alkyl halides are completely inert to sodium

Wurtz Reaction.explanation: Metallic sodium and organosodium intermediates attack esters, ketones, acids, alcohols, and amides, precluding their use in complex multi-functional synthesis.

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.question: What are the reactants in the Wurtz-Fittig reaction?

options.text: An equimolar mixture of an aryl halide and an alkyl halide with sodium metal in dry ether
Two molecules of an alkyl halide with sodium metal in dry ether
Two molecules of an aryl halide with copper powder at high temperature
An aryl halide and an alcohol with sodium hydroxide

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.explanation: The Wurtz-Fittig reaction is the coupling of an aryl halide ($Ar-X$) with an alkyl halide ($R-X$) using metallic sodium in dry ether to form an alkylarene ($Ar-R$).

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.question: What is the major product when bromobenzene and methyl bromide are treated with sodium in dry ether?
Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.explanation: Cross-coupling between bromobenzene and methyl bromide yields toluene: $C_6H_5Br + CH_3Br + 2Na \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} C_6H_5-CH_3 + 2NaBr$.

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.question: What byproducts are formed alongside toluene in the reaction of bromobenzene and methyl bromide with sodium in dry ether?

options.text: Biphenyl (from Fittig coupling) and ethane (from Wurtz coupling)

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.explanation: Self-coupling of two bromobenzene molecules yields biphenyl ($C_6H_5-C_6H_5$), while self-coupling of two methyl bromide molecules yields ethane ($CH_3-CH_3$).

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.question: Why is the Wurtz-Fittig reaction much more synthetically useful than an unsymmetrical aliphatic Wurtz reaction?

options.text: No byproducts are formed in the Wurtz-Fittig reaction
The reaction does not require any solvent
Aryl halides react 1,000 times faster than alkyl halides
The boiling points of the three products (alkylarene, volatile alkane, and high-boiling biaryl) differ substantially, allowing easy separation

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.explanation: Unlike mixtures of aliphatic alkanes with nearly identical boiling points, the volatile gaseous/low-boiling alkane, liquid alkylarene, and solid high-boiling biphenyl have widely different physical properties and are readily separated.

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.question: What is the product when bromobenzene and ethyl bromide are treated with sodium in dry ether?
Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.explanation: Cross-coupling of the phenyl radical/carbanion with the ethyl radical/halide cleanly yields ethylbenzene ($C_6H_5-CH_2CH_3$).

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.question: Which organometallic intermediate is formed first in the Wurtz-Fittig reaction?

options.text: Arylsodium ($\text{Ar-Na}$) because aryl radicals are more easily formed and arylsodium is more stable than alkylsodium

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.explanation: Sodium transfers an electron more readily to the aryl halide; the resulting arylsodium intermediate ($	ext{Ar}^-	ext{Na}^+$) then acts as a nucleophile displacing the halide from $R-X$ via an $S_N2$ pathway.

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.question: When bromobenzene and 1-bromopropane react with sodium in dry ether, the alkylarene product is:
Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.explanation: Nucleophilic displacement of bromide from 1-bromopropane by the phenyl carbanion ($C_6H_5^-$) occurs via an $S_N2$ mechanism without carbocation rearrangement, yielding n-propylbenzene.

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.question: What is the major alkylarene product when 1-bromonaphthalene and bromomethane are treated with sodium in dry ether?
Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.explanation: Cross-coupling between the 1-naphthyl group and methyl group yields 1-methylnaphthalene.

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.question: What product is obtained when p-bromotoluene and bromoethane are treated with sodium in dry ether?
Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.explanation: The 4-methylphenyl moiety couples with the ethyl group at the carbon bearing the bromine atom, producing 1-ethyl-4-methylbenzene.

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.question: Which of the following alkyl halides will give the poorest yield in a Wurtz-Fittig reaction with bromobenzene?
Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.explanation: Tertiary alkyl halides undergo rapid $E2$ elimination by the strongly basic arylsodium ($C_6H_5^-Na^+$) to give an alkene (isobutylene) and benzene, rather than the coupled product.

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.question: In the Wurtz-Fittig reaction, what happens if the reaction mixture contains moisture?

options.text: Phenol is formed as the major product
Arylsodium is protonated to benzene, and sodium metal is destroyed with evolution of $\text{H}_2$

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.explanation: Water vigorously reacts with $Na$ and rapidly protonates the strongly basic arylsodium: $C_6H_5Na + H_2O \rightarrow C_6H_6 + NaOH$.

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.question: Which of the following pairs of reactants will successfully yield isopropylbenzene (cumene) via Wurtz-Fittig reaction?

options.text: Bromobenzene and 2-bromopropane with $\text{Na}$ in dry ether

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.explanation: Cross-coupling of the phenyl moiety from bromobenzene with the 2-propyl moiety from 2-bromopropane produces cumene.

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.question: What is the primary mechanism of the cross-coupling step in the Wurtz-Fittig reaction?

options.text: $S_N2$ displacement of the alkyl halide by the arylsodium nucleophile ($\text{Ar}^- + \text{R-X} \rightarrow \text{Ar-R} + \text{X}^-$)
Electrophilic aromatic substitution of the alkyl halide by benzene

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.explanation: Arylsodium ($	ext{Ar}^-	ext{Na}^+$) functions as an organometallic nucleophile that attacks the less-hindered primary alkyl carbon from the back side, expelling the halide ion in an $S_N2$ transition state.

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.question: Which halogen derivative of benzene gives the fastest reaction in the Wurtz-Fittig reaction?
Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.explanation: Iodobenzene has the weakest carbon-halogen bond and undergoes single-electron reduction by sodium most readily.

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.question: Can fluorobenzene be efficiently used in the Wurtz-Fittig reaction?

options.text: Yes, it gives the highest yield of all haloarenes
Yes, but only in water as solvent
No, the $\text{C-F}$ bond in fluoroarenes is exceptionally unreactive toward sodium reduction

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.explanation: Due to strong $p-\pi$ overlap and high bond dissociation energy, the $C_{sp^2}-F$ bond does not cleave under standard Wurtz-Fittig conditions.

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.question: The reaction of chlorobenzene and 1-chlorobutane with sodium in dry ether gives:
Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.explanation: The primary 1-butyl group is coupled without rearrangement to the phenyl ring, yielding straight-chain n-butylbenzene.

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.question: Who discovered the modification of the Wurtz reaction involving aryl halides?
Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.explanation: Rudolph Fittig extended Charles-Adolphe Wurtz's alkane coupling to aryl halides, creating the Wurtz-Fittig and Fittig reactions in the 1860s.

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.question: Reaction of 2-chlorotoluene with methyl chloride and sodium in dry ether yields:
Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.explanation: Cross-coupling of the 2-methylphenyl radical/carbanion with methyl chloride replaces the chlorine atom with a methyl group, forming ortho-xylene.

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.question: What is the physical state of the biphenyl byproduct formed in the Wurtz-Fittig preparation of toluene?

options.text: A dark viscous tar insoluble in ether
A crystalline white solid with high melting point ($70^\circ\text{C}$) and boiling point ($255^\circ\text{C}$)

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.explanation: Biphenyl is a stable, crystalline aromatic solid that readily crystallizes or remains in the distillation pot while toluene ($bp\ 110.6^\circ C$) distills off.

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.question: Which of the following solvents CANNOT replace dry diethyl ether in the Wurtz-Fittig reaction?
Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.explanation: Ethanol has an acidic proton ($pK_a \approx 16$) that reacts vigorously with sodium to evolve $H_2$ and protonates arylsodium to benzene.

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.question: Treatment of bromobenzene, 1,4-dibromobutane, and sodium in dry ether in a 2:1 molar ratio yields:
Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.explanation: Both terminal bromides of 1,4-dibromobutane undergo cross-coupling with two phenyl units to form 1,4-diphenylbutane ($C_6H_5-(CH_2)_4-C_6H_5$).

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.question: Why is an excess of alkyl halide often employed over the aryl halide in the Wurtz-Fittig reaction?

options.text: To make the sodium dissolve completely
To favor cross-coupling with the arylsodium intermediate and suppress homocoupling to biphenyl
To prevent the ether from boiling away
To neutralize the basic sodium halide

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.explanation: Maintaining a high local concentration of the alkyl halide ensures that the generated arylsodium rapidly attacks $R-X$ before it can react with unreduced aryl halide to form biphenyl.

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.question: Can Wurtz-Fittig reaction be carried out using an acyl chloride instead of an alkyl halide?

options.text: Yes, it yields aromatic ketones cleanly
Yes, it is another name for Friedel-Crafts acylation
No, acyl chlorides react with sodium to undergo acyloin condensation or decompose violently
Yes, but only in aqueous acid

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.explanation: Acyl chlorides possess a reactive carbonyl group that reacts non-selectively with active metals, destroying the reagent.

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.question: Reaction of 4-chlorobiphenyl with methyl chloride and sodium in dry ether yields:
Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.explanation: Cross-coupling of the 4-biphenylyl fragment with methyl chloride replaces the chloro group with a methyl group to give 4-methylbiphenyl.

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.question: What gas is formed as a byproduct during the Wurtz-Fittig synthesis of ethylbenzene using ethyl bromide?
Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.explanation: Homocoupling of ethyl bromide ($2C_2H_5Br + 2Na \rightarrow C_4H_{10} + 2NaBr$) yields butane, which boils at $-0.5^\circ C$ and easily separates from ethylbenzene ($bp\ 136^\circ C$).

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.question: Which of the following compounds CANNOT be prepared by the Wurtz-Fittig reaction?
Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.explanation: Diphenyl ether is an ether ($Ar-O-Ar$), not an alkylarene; ethers are synthesized via Williamson ether synthesis or Ullmann condensation, not Wurtz-Fittig coupling.

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.question: When an optically active alkyl halide, such as $(R)\text{-2-bromooctane}$, is subjected to Wurtz-Fittig reaction with bromobenzene, the product 2-phenyloctane shows:

options.text: Predominant inversion of configuration via the $S_N2$ pathway

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.explanation: Because nucleophilic attack of arylsodium ($	ext{Ar}^-$) on the secondary alkyl halide proceeds primarily by back-side $S_N2$ displacement, inversion of stereochemistry is predominantly observed.

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.question: What is the product when 1-bromo-4-chlorobenzene is treated with 1 equivalent of methyl iodide and 2 equivalents of sodium in dry ether?
Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.explanation: Because the $C-Br$ bond is significantly weaker than the $C-Cl$ bond, single-electron reduction occurs selectively at the bromine-bearing carbon, yielding 4-chlorotoluene.

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.question: Which of the following metals can promote the Wurtz-Fittig coupling in place of sodium?
Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.explanation: Lithium readily reduces aryl and alkyl halides in ether to form aryllithium intermediates that couple efficiently with alkyl halides.

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.question: The reaction between bromobenzene, benzyl bromide, and sodium in dry ether affords:
Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.explanation: Cross-coupling between the phenyl group ($C_6H_5-$) and benzyl group ($C_6H_5CH_2-$) yields diphenylmethane ($C_6H_5-CH_2-C_6H_5$).

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.question: Why is the Wurtz-Fittig reaction rarely used for coupling secondary or tertiary alkyl halides?

options.text: Secondary alkyl halides do not dissolve in ether
Aryl halides cannot react in the presence of branched alkanes
Elimination ($E2$) dominates over substitution due to the high basicity of arylsodium

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.explanation: Arylsodium is a very strong Brønsted base that abstracts a $ eta$-hydrogen from secondary and tertiary halides via $E2$ elimination, generating alkenes and benzene.

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.question: What is the role of sodium in the Wurtz-Fittig reaction?

options.text: It serves as a dehydrating agent
It acts as an electrophilic catalyst
It stabilizes the ether solvent against oxidation
It acts as a single-electron reducing agent that cleaves carbon-halogen bonds heterolytically/homolytically

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.explanation: Sodium donates its valence electron to the $\sigma^*$ orbital of the $C-X$ bond, initiating homolytic cleavage and forming organosodium species.

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.question: Coupling of bromobenzene with allyl bromide in the presence of sodium in dry ether yields:
Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.explanation: Cross-coupling of the phenyl ring with the primary allyl carbon gives allylbenzene ($C_6H_5-CH_2-CH=CH_2$).

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.question: In the Wurtz-Fittig reaction, if the temperature is allowed to rise too high, what side reaction becomes prominent?

options.text: Polymerization, tarring, and extensive radical disproportionation
Conversion of alkylarenes to carboxylic acids

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.explanation: Excessive heating causes uncontrolled radical side reactions, waxy hydrocarbon polymers, and loss of ether solvent.

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.question: Which of the following statements about the Fittig and Wurtz-Fittig reactions is TRUE?

options.text: Both reactions use copper powder exclusively
Wurtz-Fittig reaction yields symmetrical biaryls as the only product
Fittig reaction involves two aryl halides; Wurtz-Fittig involves one aryl halide and one alkyl halide
Fittig reaction is used to prepare aliphatic alkanes

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.explanation: Fittig homocouples two aryl halides to biaryls ($Ar-Ar$), whereas Wurtz-Fittig cross-couples an aryl halide and an alkyl halide to alkylarenes ($Ar-R$).

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.question: What is the product when bromobenzene is reacted with 1-bromo-2-phenylethane and sodium in dry ether?
Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.explanation: Cross-coupling of phenyl ($C_6H_5-$) with 2-phenylethyl ($-CH_2CH_2C_6H_5$) produces 1,2-diphenylethane (bibenzyl).

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.question: Treatment of o-bromochlorobenzene with magnesium or sodium can yield benzyne. In a standard Wurtz-Fittig reaction with an isolated mono-haloarene, benzyne formation is:

options.text: Avoided because monohaloarenes lack the leaving group at the ortho position required for elimination

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.explanation: Simple monohaloarenes undergo single electron transfer to form aryl radicals/anions without benzyne elimination because there is no leaving group ortho to the carbanion.

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.question: When bromobenzene reacts with chloromethane and sodium in dry ether, the halogen eliminated as precipitate is:

options.text: A mixture of sodium bromide ($\text{NaBr}$) and sodium chloride ($\text{NaCl}$)

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.explanation: The bromine from bromobenzene and chlorine from chloromethane both combine with sodium to form insoluble precipitates of $NaBr$ and $NaCl$.

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.question: Why is the reaction mixture in the Wurtz-Fittig reaction typically filtered after completion?

options.text: To collect the alkylarene as a solid on the filter paper
To separate the ether from the products
To remove the insoluble precipitated sodium halides ($\text{NaX}$) and unreacted sodium before fractional distillation
To prevent oxidation of the aromatic ring

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.explanation: Sodium halides ($NaCl, NaBr$) are completely insoluble in dry ether and form a suspension; filtration separates these inorganic salts from the organic ether solution.

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.question: What safety precaution is mandatory when quenching unreacted sodium metal after a Wurtz-Fittig reaction?

options.text: Pouring large volumes of cold water directly into the flask
Dumping the mixture into the open trash
Carefully adding isopropanol or ethanol in a well-ventilated hood to destroy sodium slowly, NEVER water directly

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.explanation: Active sodium reacts violently and explosively with water; it must be destroyed smoothly with a secondary alcohol like isopropanol, which evolves hydrogen at a moderate, controllable rate.

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.question: Which of the following is an example of an intramolecular Wurtz-Fittig-type reaction?

options.text: Reaction of 1-bromo-2-(2-bromoethyl)benzene with sodium to give indane
Reaction of bromobenzene with ethyl bromide
Reaction of benzyl chloride with sodium

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.explanation: Having an aryl bromide and an alkyl bromide in the same molecule allows intramolecular coupling to close a fused cyclopentane ring, forming indane.

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.question: What happens if dry benzene is used as a co-solvent with ether in the Wurtz-Fittig reaction?

options.text: Benzene undergoes instant coupling with itself
It works well because benzene is an unreactive aromatic hydrocarbon under these conditions

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.explanation: Benzene has no halogen or reactive functional group; it acts as an inert hydrocarbon solvent alongside ether.

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.question: Cross-coupling of 2-bromonaphthalene with ethyl bromide and sodium in dry ether gives:
Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.explanation: The 2-naphthyl radical/carbanion cross-couples with the ethyl group to give 2-ethylnaphthalene.

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.question: Which of the following pairs of reactants would yield sec-butylbenzene via Wurtz-Fittig reaction?

options.text: Bromobenzene and 1-bromobutane with $\text{Na}$ in dry ether
Bromobenzene and 2-bromobutane with $\text{Na}$ in dry ether

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.explanation: Direct cross-coupling of bromobenzene with 2-bromobutane introduces the sec-butyl moiety onto the phenyl ring.

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.question: What is the formal role of the aryl halide in the cross-coupling mechanism of the Wurtz-Fittig reaction?

options.text: It acts as the precursor to the nucleophilic arylsodium reagent via reduction by sodium
It acts as an electrophile attacked by an alkyl radical
It acts as a Brønsted acid
It acts as a phase-transfer catalyst

Wurtz-Fittig Reaction.explanation: The aryl halide is reduced by sodium to generate the carbanionic nucleophile ($	ext{Ar}^-	ext{Na}^+$), which performs nucleophilic displacement on the alkyl halide.

Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis.question: What is the primary synthetic utility of Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis?

options.text: Preparation of pure primary ($1^\circ$) aliphatic amines without contamination by $2^\circ$ or $3^\circ$ amines
Preparation of aromatic primary amines like aniline
Preparation of secondary and tertiary amines

Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis.explanation: Gabriel synthesis is specifically used for the synthesis of pure primary aliphatic amines. Since the intermediate $N$-alkylphthalimide cannot undergo further alkylation, no secondary or tertiary amines or quaternary ammonium salts are formed.

Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis.question: What are the sequential steps in the Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis?

options.text: Reduction of phthalimide with $\text{LiAlH}_4$, followed by alkylation
Deprotonation of phthalimide by alcoholic $\text{KOH}$, nucleophilic substitution ($S_N2$) of alkyl halide by potassium phthalimide, and alkaline hydrolysis or hydrazinolysis of $N$-alkylphthalimide
Reaction of phthalimide with ammonia and bromine

Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis.explanation: Phthalimide is deprotonated by $\text{KOH}$ to give potassium phthalimide, which undergoes $S_N2$ displacement with a $1^\circ$ alkyl halide to form $N$-alkylphthalimide. Hydrolysis or treatment with hydrazine cleaves the phthaloyl ring to release pure $1^\circ$ amine.

Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis.question: Why is phthalimide acidic enough to form a salt with potassium hydroxide ($\text{KOH}$)?

options.text: Phthalimide contains an inorganic acid radical
The hydrogen on the imide nitrogen is flanked by two strongly electron-withdrawing carbonyl groups, and the resulting conjugate base is resonance-stabilized over both carbonyl oxygens

Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis.explanation: The imide hydrogen has a $pK_a \approx 8.3$. Resonance delocalization of the negative charge across both carbonyl oxygens makes the conjugate phthalimide anion exceptionally stable and easy to form using alcoholic $\text{KOH}$.

Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis.question: Why CANNOT aromatic primary amines (like aniline) be prepared by Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis?

options.text: Aniline is unstable in basic medium
Potassium phthalimide decomposes in the presence of aromatic rings
Aniline forms an explosive gas with phthalimide

Aryl halides (like chlorobenzene or bromobenzene) do not undergo nucleophilic substitution ($S_N2$) with potassium phthalimide due to resonance partial double-bond character and steric repulsion of the benzene ring

Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis.explanation: Potassium phthalimide is a bulky nucleophile that attacks via $S_N2$. Aryl halides are inert toward $S_N2$ displacement because the $\text{C}_{\text{Ar}}-\text{X}$ bond has partial double-bond character and the ring repels nucleophilic attack.

Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis.question: Which of the following amines CANNOT be prepared by Gabriel phthalimide synthesis?
Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis.explanation: Aniline cannot be prepared because it would require bromobenzene as the alkylating agent, which cannot undergo $S_N2$ substitution with potassium phthalimide.

Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis.question: Can benzylamine ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$) be synthesized by Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis?

options.text: No, because benzylamine has an aromatic benzene ring
Yes, because benzyl chloride is a primary benzylic halide that undergoes facile $S_N2$ displacement with potassium phthalimide
No, because benzyl chloride is an aryl halide
Yes, but only in the presence of $\text{AlCl}_3$

Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis.explanation: The halogen in benzyl chloride is attached to an aliphatic $\text{sp}^3$ benzylic carbon, not directly to the aromatic ring; it undergoes rapid $S_N2$ displacement by potassium phthalimide to yield benzylamine cleanly.

Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis.question: Why is hydrazine ($\text{NH}_2\text{NH}_2$, Ing-Manske procedure) frequently used instead of aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ to cleave $N$-alkylphthalimides?

options.text: Because sodium hydroxide destroys the primary amine
Because hydrazine turns the product into a gas
Hydrazinolysis occurs much faster under neutral/mild conditions and precipitates insoluble phthalhydrazide, isolating the free primary amine under non-harsh conditions
Because hydrazine acts as an oxidizing agent

Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis.explanation: The Ing-Manske modification uses hydrazine hydrate in refluxing ethanol; the highly nucleophilic hydrazine rapidly cleaves both imide amide bonds, precipitating phthalhydrazide and liberating the $1^\circ$ amine in excellent yields.

Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis.question: What type of alkyl halide gives poor or negligible yield of primary amine in Gabriel synthesis?

options.text: Tertiary ($3^\circ$) alkyl halides, because they undergo $E2$ elimination exclusively to form alkenes instead of substitution

Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis.explanation: Potassium phthalimide is a moderately strong base; tertiary halides undergo rapid $E2$ elimination to give alkenes rather than the $S_N2$ substitution needed for amine formation.

Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis.question: What is the product when potassium phthalimide is treated with 2-bromopropane?

options.text: Isopropylamine (accompanied by propene from competing $E2$ elimination)

Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis.explanation: Secondary halides undergo both $S_N2$ substitution and $E2$ elimination, giving moderate yields of isopropylamine along with propene.

Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis.question: What byproduct is formed during the alkaline hydrolysis of $N$-alkylphthalimide with aqueous $\text{NaOH}$?
Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis.explanation: Alkaline hydrolysis cleaves both imide $\text{C-N}$ bonds, producing disodium phthalate ($o-\text{C}_6\text{H}_4(\text{COONa})_2$) and the free primary amine ($R\text{NH}_2$).

Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis.question: What is the molecular formula of phthalimide?
Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis.explanation: Phthalimide consists of a benzene ring fused to a 5-membered cyclic imide ring: $\text{C}_6\text{H}_4(\text{CO})_2\text{NH} = \text{C}_8\text{H}_5\text{NO}_2$.

Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis.question: How is phthalimide synthesized industrially?

options.text: By heating phthalic anhydride with concentrated ammonia ($\text{NH}_3$) or ammonium carbonate

Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis.explanation: Heating phthalic anhydride with aqueous ammonia initially forms phthalamic acid, which upon strong heating loses water to close the imide ring, producing phthalimide.

Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis.question: Which of the following halides will react FASTEST with potassium phthalimide?
Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis.explanation: In $S_N2$ reactions, methyl halides have zero steric hindrance and iodide is the best leaving group, making methyl iodide the most reactive substrate.

Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis.question: Can neopentyl amine be prepared in high yield using Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis?

options.text: Yes, it gives a $100\%$ yield easily
No, because neopentyl bromide is severely sterically hindered by the $\beta$-tert-butyl group, making $S_N2$ backside attack by phthalimide extremely sluggish
No, because neopentyl amine is unstable
Yes, using potassium metal as catalyst

Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis.explanation: Neopentyl halides are primary but experience immense steric hindrance toward backside nucleophilic attack, making Gabriel synthesis ineffective.

Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis.question: What amino acid can be synthesized using a modified Gabriel synthesis using diethyl bromomalonate?
Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis.explanation: The Gabriel-malonic ester synthesis alkylates potassium phthalimide with diethyl bromomalonate; subsequent alkylation, hydrolysis, and decarboxylation yields racemic $\alpha$-amino acids.

Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis.question: What is the product when potassium phthalimide is reacted with chloroacetic acid, followed by acid hydrolysis?
Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis.explanation: Displacement of chloride by phthalimide followed by hydrolysis of the imide bonds yields glycine (aminoacetic acid).

Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis.question: What is the hybridization of the nitrogen atom in the phthalimide anion?
Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis.explanation: The negative charge on nitrogen is delocalized into the adjacent $\pi$ systems of both carbonyl groups; to maximize overlap, the nitrogen atom adopts planar $\text{sp}^2$ hybridization.

Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis.question: Why is Gabriel synthesis superior to direct alkylation of ammonia (Hofmann's ammonolysis) for preparing primary amines?

options.text: Gabriel synthesis does not require heat

Direct ammonolysis of alkyl halides leads to over-alkylation giving complex mixtures of $1^\circ, 2^\circ, 3^\circ$ amines and $4^\circ$ salts, whereas Gabriel synthesis cleanly produces only $1^\circ$ amine
Ammonia does not react with alkyl halides
Hofmann ammonolysis destroys the alkyl group
